title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding
abstract: Streaming video understanding is a critical capability for real-world applications, including embodied intelligence, autonomous driving, industrial monitoring, surveillance and early warning, and wearable assistants. However, processing continuous video streams with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is computationally expensive. Existing efforts have explored reducing streaming overhead through visual token pruning, token merging, quantization, on-demand frame retrieval, and context offloading. However, most existing methods overlook the dimension of model depth. Repeatedly executing full-depth MLLM prefill over incoming frames is prohibitively expensive, incurring substantial computational overhead and causing the KV cache to grow at a rate directly proportional to the prefill depth. To address these challenges, we propose ShallowStream, a novel framework that leverages the shallow layers of an MLLM to simultaneously perform frame encoding and retrieval index building. During stream processing, ShallowStream maintains an always-on lightweight index using the KV cache of shallow layers. During query-time answering, we leverage the attention scores generated by the shallow layers to score context frames and employ a diversity-aware selection strategy to retrieve precise and comprehensive evidence. ShallowStream achieves performance on par with the strongest existing streaming methods, while reducing per-frame prefill latency and 10-second end-to-end latency by up to 52.1x and 11.9x, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/CURRENTF/ShallowStream.

title: PARA: The four faculties, their authority types, and the loop
abstract: Four faculties defined by what each may read and write. Perception has read-only access to system signals, writes nothing outside its observation stream, emits structured observations, and must distinguish what was measured from what was inferred. Reasoning has read access to observations and runbooks, writes nothing at all, and emits a plan with the justification that supports it; it must also be able to conclude that no action is warranted, and that conclusion is recorded with the same weight as a plan. Action holds the sole authority to change production, through enumerated policy-authorized operations only, and records the operation as performed rather than as planned. Adaptation writes to institutional knowledge and never to production, and each adaptation cites the observations, plan and outcome it derives from. Two faculties write and two do not, and the two that write are the two that carry guardrails. The acronym reads P-A-R-A while the loop runs perception, reasoning, action, adaptation; reasoning precedes action so that a justification is not constructed afterwards, which would be a rationalization indistinguishable from a justification in the record. This figure is Figure 1 of PARA: Perception, Action, Reasoning, Adaptation, version 1.0, deposited at Zenodo. title: Operationalising the Six Diagnostic Questions: A Scorecard for Architectural Succession and a Formal Statement of the Unstoppable AI Hypothesis Volume II of the KSCCN Working Paper Series on Architectural Diagnostics
abstract: Volume I anatomised six diagnostic questions (Pagidyala, 2026) and stated an Unstoppable AI Hypothesis (UAIH): architectural succession is compatible with field-level continuation (Mamun, 2026a). Anatomy without measurement, however, remains a vocabulary. This second volume converts the six questions into an operational scorecard with observable indicators, explicit non-compensatory interpretation rules, and documented Goodhart risks. Question 1 is grounded in the continual-learning matrix of Lopez-Paz and Ranzato (2017)—average accuracy, backward transfer and forward transfer—extended by cost, latency and non-reset conditions that laboratory task-incremental suites omit. Questions 2–6 receive production-function, construct-validity, unit-cost, scaffold-ratio and obsolescence-of-role indicators. UAIH is then restated in the language of general-purpose-technology growth (Bresnahan and Trajtenberg, 1995; Helpman and Trajtenberg, 1994, 1998): conditions C1–C4 become empirical predicates, and a local-versus-global winter test is defined on deployment, complementary capital and capability stocks rather than on equity narratives. A first qualitative application scores the incumbent frozen-foundation stack against an experience-compounding programme class. The incumbent leads on present static benchmarks and installed capital; the contrasting class leads, where evidence exists, on the learning-loop criteria the six questions isolate. Neither score is a vendor ranking. Also available on Academia.edu: https://www.academia.edu/attachments/134108536/download_file?s=portfolio

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A State of the Art Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Adaptive Neural Network Self-Organization Learning (ANNSL)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Neural Network Self-Organization Learning (ANNSL), a novel framework for self-organizing learning based on adaptive neural network architectures. Traditional self-organizing learning approaches often require manual parameter tuning, limiting flexibility and potentially hindering the model's ability to discover optimal representations. ANNSL leverages the inherent properties of adaptive neural networks – specifically, their ability to dynamically adjust connection strengths and weights – to foster self-organization. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously optimizes the network's structure through iterative adjustments, resulting in enhanced feature extraction and representation learning. This paper details the design of ANNSL, presents preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness, and explores potential applications within various machine learning domains.

title: Title: Embedding Quantum States within a Higher-Dimensional Lattice
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging higher-dimensional lattices to represent and manipulate quantum states. Quantum mechanics often struggles with the computational complexity of directly mapping complex quantum systems to finite-dimensional spaces. We propose a method for embedding quantum states within a lattice structure, aiming to simplify the analysis and computation of quantum phenomena. This involves constructing a lattice with specific properties that facilitate entanglement and superposition, allowing for a more intuitive and manageable representation of quantum states. The core mechanism focuses on designing a lattice topology that inherently supports these properties, offering a novel approach to exploring quantum mechanics in a higher-dimensional setting. The research explores the theoretical foundations and potential applications of this technique, highlighting its promise for advancing our understanding of quantum systems and offering a pathway towards more efficient quantum computation.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Modular Arithmetic for Cryptography
abstract: Quantum-enhanced modular arithmetic presents a revolutionary approach to cryptography, capitalizing on the unique properties of quantum mechanics to create fundamentally more secure keys. This paper investigates the implementation of a novel quantum-based 'entangled parity' operation, demonstrating its potential to substantially improve the security of cryptographic keys through enhanced resistance to known attacks. We explore the core mechanism of this system, outlining its potential to significantly reduce computational overhead while bolstering resistance to brute-force attacks and other established vulnerabilities. The research focuses on demonstrating a practical implementation and showcasing the advantages of this quantum-enhanced approach compared to traditional methods.

title: Quantum-Inspired Distributed Memory Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel architecture for distributed memory networks inspired by the principles of quantum superposition and entanglement. Traditional distributed memory systems struggle with scalability and efficiency when dealing with large datasets and complex pattern recognition tasks. Our approach addresses these limitations by leveraging probabilistic representations of data nodes, mimicking quantum amplitudes, which enable multiple simultaneous representations and correlations. A key component is the "entanglement protocol," designed to facilitate efficient information sharing and accelerate retrieval processes across the network. The core claim of this work is to demonstrate exponentially faster information retrieval and pattern recognition capabilities compared to conventional distributed memory models. We outline the theoretical framework, detailing the mathematical formulations underlying the network architecture and the entanglement protocol. The proposed system offers a fundamentally different paradigm for data storage and access, moving beyond classical constraints and potentially unlocking significant performance gains in data-intensive applications.

title: Algorithmic Fairness via Randomized Smoothing in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, the inherent data heterogeneity and potential biases present in these datasets pose significant challenges to achieving algorithmic fairness. This paper investigates the application of randomized smoothing, a technique traditionally used in batch learning, to mitigate bias and improve fairness in federated learning settings. We propose a novel framework that adapts randomized smoothing to the asynchronous and decentralized nature of FL. The core idea is to introduce controlled noise during model aggregation, effectively averaging out biased updates from clients with differing data distributions. Our approach demonstrates improved fairness metrics compared to standard federated averaging, particularly in scenarios with significant data skew. We formally define the problem, outline the methodology, and discuss the theoretical implications of our findings. This work represents a new direction in fairness-aware federated learning and contributes to the development of more robust and equitable machine learning systems.

title: Differential Privacy via Information-Theoretic Compression
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to differential privacy that leverages information-theoretic compression techniques. The core argument is that existing differential privacy methods often introduce excessive noise, degrading model utility. We introduce a framework where data is preprocessed using algorithms like the Burrows-Wheeler transform and wavelet compression, effectively creating a noise layer *before* the application of traditional differential privacy mechanisms. This approach aims to achieve stronger privacy guarantees while minimizing the impact on information utility. We demonstrate, theoretically, that this strategy aligns with the principles of information theory, offering a more efficient and potentially more robust method for preserving privacy in machine learning models. The key contribution lies in shifting the role of noise from a purely additive process to a strategically applied, compression-based layer. This reduces the overall noise level and preserves more of the underlying information, leading to a more practical and effective solution for privacy-preserving data analysis.

title: Probability Logic Adaptive Algorithm: A Deep Learning Fusion
abstract: This paper investigates a novel probabilistic logic system leveraging adaptive algorithms and deep learning integration. Traditional probabilistic reasoning relies heavily on manually crafted rules, limiting adaptability and scalability. This work proposes a framework that dynamically learns and incorporates probabilistic logic features extracted from deep neural networks, enhancing reasoning capabilities. The core mechanism centers around deep learning-driven feature extraction and integration, resulting in a system capable of handling complex scenarios and exhibiting improved accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional approaches. This research explores the potential of deep learning to augment and enhance probabilistic reasoning, paving the way for more robust and adaptable systems.

title: Quantum Topological Error Correction Protocol (QTE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Quantum Topological Error Correction Protocol (QTE) designed to achieve highly reliable correction of quantum information during transmission, thereby significantly enhancing the fault-tolerance capabilities of quantum computation. The core of the protocol leverages the synergistic combination of quantum topological protection and advanced error-correcting codes. Specifically, we introduce a protocol based on topologically protected qubits and a tailored error-correcting code. The topological protection mechanism mitigates the detrimental effects of local noise, while the error-correcting code handles residual errors that remain after topological protection. This layered approach provides a robust defense against quantum errors, offering a pathway toward scalable and reliable quantum computation. The key innovation lies in minimizing reliance on classical communication, a significant bottleneck in traditional quantum error correction schemes, and in maximizing correction efficiency through the inherent properties of topological protection. The protocol utilizes a structured approach to error detection and correction, employing a multi-stage process for enhanced reliability. Mathematical formalism is presented to detail the protocol's operation and performance. ---

title: Quantum Simulation of Nonlinear Patterns Recognition
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a novel approach to studying complex quantum systems and their underlying nonlinear behaviors. This research investigates the potential of quantum simulation to identify and characterize these patterns, providing a powerful tool for advancing our understanding of quantum phenomena. The core claim is that by utilizing quantum simulation, we can effectively discern subtle nonlinear patterns within quantum systems, ultimately revealing fundamental principles governing their behavior. This work will explore various simulation techniques and their impact on pattern recognition, focusing on identifying key nonlinear features through the analysis of quantum states.

title: Context-Aware Probabilistic Programming with Latent Variable Dynamics
abstract: Probabilistic programming has emerged as a powerful paradigm for building and reasoning about probabilistic models. However, a significant limitation lies in its difficulty in effectively handling complex systems characterized by dynamic latent variables and intricate dependencies between them. This paper introduces a novel "Context-Aware" probabilistic programming system designed to overcome this challenge. The core mechanism integrates a latent variable dynamics model, typically a variant of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), conditioned on both observed data and contextual information. This allows for the simulation of evolving probabilistic systems, capturing the temporal evolution of latent variables. The system's ability to incorporate contextual information provides a crucial enhancement, enabling the modeling of systems where the dynamics are influenced by external factors. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline the key components and design considerations for such a system. The proposed methodology offers a significant advancement in probabilistic modeling, providing a robust tool for uncertainty quantification and predictive modeling in complex, dynamic scenarios.

title: Title: Topological Geometry Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on topological geometry, designed to dynamically adjust system parameters based on internal structural characteristics. Traditional optimization algorithms typically rely on manual parameter adjustment, whereas this approach leverages machine learning to learn and adapt system parameters in real-time. The core mechanism involves training a model to represent the system's topology and then utilizing this model to iteratively refine parameters, leading to improved optimization performance. This work addresses a key limitation of existing optimization techniques: the need for extensive manual tuning. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, demonstrates its efficacy through illustrative examples, and discusses its potential applications across various fields.

title: 基于自适应的图论算法的拓扑优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to data clustering based on an adaptive graph theory algorithm. Traditional data clustering methods often rely on static parameters, failing to effectively adapt to data distribution shifts. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the graph structure to optimize data clustering, resulting in enhanced data quality and improved clustering performance. We introduce a learning-based framework that learns a representation of the data's underlying structure and uses this representation to iteratively refine the graph topology, ensuring optimal clustering. This adaptive approach significantly outperforms traditional methods in various datasets.

title: BioEdge-RGC: Compact Neural Policy Transfer from Model-Predictive Control in a Transcriptomics-Informed Optic Nerve Injury Simulation
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Optic nerve injury involves heterogeneous neuronal and microenvironmental responses that may require sequential, state-dependent intervention. BioEdge-RGC was developed as a transcriptomics-informed computational benchmark for transferring a globally planned model-predictive-control policy to compact regional neural models operating with incomplete observations and reduced communication. METHODS: Public mouse optic-nerve-crush transcriptomic datasets were summarized into seven retinal ganglion cell modules and eight retinal environment modules and fused into a 15-dimensional temporal reference state for a 16-region, five-step simulator. A candidate-constrained MPC expert was approximated by a central neural teacher and local, neighbour-aware, and coordinated regional students trained using hybrid knowledge distillation or direct MPC supervision. Missing observations, severe simulated injury, INT8 quantization, local parameter perturbations, and an independent GSE229033 transcriptomic plausibility assessment were evaluated. RESULTS: The central teacher retained 99.90% of the MPC objective, and the coordinated distilled student retained 99.69% of teacher performance while reducing modeled communication from 5520 to 1080 bytes per episode. The coordinated-versus-local mean-objective difference was +0.000053 and did not meet the predefined +0.008 threshold; direct MPC supervision performed at least as well as hybrid distillation. title: A Lightweight Satellite Orbit Anomaly Detection Method Based on Peak-AAE and Its Edge Deployment
abstract: The detection of orbital anomalies is of critical importance to the safe operation of on-orbit spacecraft. Existing methods often rely on manually engineered features and are constrained by the limited computational resources of satellite equipment. This paper proposes a lightweight unsupervised anomaly detection method based on the Peak Adversarial Autoencoder (Peak-AAE). First, the Peak-AAE model is employed to reconstruct historical semi-major axis data, and the squared differences between the reconstructed and original data are taken as the residual sequence. The Automatic Multi-Scale Peak Detection (AMPD) algorithm is then applied to the residual sequence to identify anomalous points. In comparison with traditional approaches, this method eliminates the need for manual feature design. Moreover, the improved Peak-AAE model effectively reduces the false positive rate associated with the original AAE model, thereby enhancing detection accuracy. Finally, the compressed Peak-AAE model is deployed on edge devices for ground simulation verification. Experimental validation on the BEIDOU-3 G2 and IRNSS-1A satellites demonstrates that the Peak-AAE model achieves a minimum precision of 90.00% and a minimum recall of 84.74%.

title: Seismoacoustic recovery of the SpaceX CRS-32 Dragon re-entry with a proof-of-concept for automated detection
abstract: Atmospheric re-entries of human-made objects are increasing in frequency, yet detailed information on their trajectory, fragmentation, and debris footprint is rarely made publicly available. This creates an information asymmetry in which regulators, independent agencies, and the scientific community lack the means to verify that re-entries occurred as reported or to characterize their physical processes for future modeling. We address this gap by applying a seismoacoustic localization method to the 25 May 2025 re-entry of the SpaceX CRS-32 Cargo Dragon spacecraft which splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Southern California. Using openly available seismic waveform data from 5 networks, including 22 Raspberry Shake amateur instruments, we recover a re-entry trajectory consistent in trajectory with the operator's publicly communicated splashdown prediction and release the manually labeled CRS-32 labeled N-wave picks as a public dataset. As a preliminary step toward automation, we train a neural network on the manually picked dataset and demonstrate reliable onset detection with stable performance across a wide range of detection thresholds, showcasing promise for N-wave detection from a two-event training set. These results show that existing open seismic infrastructure can provide independent, continental-scale characterization of re-entry events: a capability increasingly needed as the rate and opacity of commercial re-entries continue to grow.

title: Improving Clinical Target Volume Segmentation Accuracy using Anatomical Priors and Active Learning for the AGITG TOPGEAR Clinical Trial
abstract: Training deep learning-based medical image segmentation models is challenging with limited curated datasets. For AGITG TOPGEAR, a gastric cancer trial, the Clinical Target Volume (CTV) is complex and defined by multiple anatomical landmarks, making upfront training data preparation difficult for an automated contour QA segmentation model. We investigate anatomical priors, derived from surrounding organ segmentations, to provide spatial context and improve TOPGEAR CTV segmentation accuracy. We also evaluate active learning, iteratively expanding the training dataset by selecting cases expected to improve performance. One hundred TOPGEAR CT scans were retrospectively analyzed. An initial set of 10 expert-contoured cases was used to train an nnU-Net model. TotalSegmentator generated a voxel-wise anatomical prior map from surrounding structures as an additional input channel. Active learning was simulated over four iterations, selecting cases by model uncertainty and segmentation performance. All models used five-fold cross-validation for an ensemble uncertainty measure. Evaluation used a hold-out testing set of 50 cases. The anatomical prior improved CTV segmentation accuracy, increasing mean Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) from 0.84 to 0.86. Active learning similarly improved performance to 0.86, with greatest benefit in the final round. Combining the anatomical prior with active learning achieved the highest accuracy, with a DSC of 0.87. Model uncertainty correlated with DSC, supporting its use in identifying suboptimal predictions and guiding active learning. Anatomical priors and active learning each improved CTV segmentation accuracy and generalizability, with their combination achieving the best performance, supporting integration into segmentation model development for automated contour QA in radiotherapy clinical trials.

title: Balancing Frequencies and Pixels in Flow Matching
abstract: Natural images follow a $1/f^2$ spectral distribution: most signal energy lies in the low spatial frequencies, while the perceptually important structures such as textures and edges occupy sparse high-frequency bands. Pixel-space reconstruction objectives, however, treat all spatial errors uniformly, causing low frequencies to dominate the optimization signal and delaying the learning of fine-scale details. In this work, we identify this objective-level spectral imbalance as a key inefficiency in training pixel-space flow models. To address it, we propose a Focal Log-Frequency Loss (f-loss), a spectrally balanced objective that equalizes the learning signal across frequencies, emphasizing high-frequency components that are otherwise underrepresented in pixel-space objectives. Building on this, we introduce a simple training strategy that combines frequency and pixel supervision: we first emphasize frequency-domain learning early to capture all frequencies, and then transition to standard pixel-space v-loss for spatial refinement. This balancing mitigates the low-frequency bias of pixel losses and aligns the training signal with the evolving needs of the model. Our approach is conceptually simple, requires no architectural changes, and acts as a drop-in replacement for flow matching losses. Across multiple model scales, it accelerates convergence by up to 40% while consistently improving FID and perceptual fidelity.

title: Logarithmic-scale variational quantum eigensolver for off-lattice protein structure prediction in continuous torsional angle space
abstract: Classical and current quantum approaches to protein structure prediction (QPSP) face limitations, notably massive qubit requirements restricting near-term models to simplistic on-lattice simulations. We propose a logarithmic-scale variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) that reduces qubit requirements for N torsional degrees of freedom to O(log2N), enabling off-lattice, all-atom simulations. Our architecture extracts molecular torsions from relative phases in statevector simulations. On quantum hardware, a decoder maps the empirical cumulative distribution function (CDF) from basis-state probabilities to bounded torsional variables. These feed a classical algorithm to build heavy-atom coordinates. We use an EfficientSU2 ansatz and multi-stage relaxation to mitigate barren plateaus. Structures are evaluated via a custom hybrid quantum-classical Hamiltonian, alongside Rosetta and OpenMM benchmarks. Evaluation on chignolin and Trp-cage yielded native-like conformations. Chignolin reached a 0.623 Å Cα RMSD in retained snapshots and 1.199 Å in final models; Trp-cage achieved a 2.501 Å RMSD among snapshots (3.512 Å in final models). Execution on IBM processors (ibm_cleveland, ibm_miami) successfully recovered native-like structures with a best RMSD of 1.758 Å. The custom energy function performed best overall, though energy-ranking imbalances persisted across sampled landscapes for all functions. This introduces the first all-atom, continuous-space quantum algorithm for QPSP. By converting physical qubit constraints into circuit depth constraints, it proves high-resolution prediction is feasible with exponentially fewer qubits. Despite current limits like computational overhead and energy function sensitivity, it establishes a scalable foundation for hybrid quantum biophysics.

title: Train What You Deploy: Closing the MLP Reachability Gap in Low-Rank Clone Distillation
abstract: A compressed student has two shapes that need not agree: the weight it deploys at inference and the weight family its training can reach. We show that a state-of-the-art weight-inheritance distiller, Low-Rank Clone (LRC), deploys a full-width student MLP but ties training to a teacher-induced slice, leaving 62.5-81.4% of each deployed matrix's independent linear degrees of freedom unreachable-paid for at inference, never trainable. Our principle is one line: train what you deploy. From the identical LRC warm start, we make the training object the entire deployed matrix, with no change in deployed shape, deployed parameter count, or inference FLOPs, via two mergeable realizations (Dense-LRC and CORE-LRC) that both collapse to one deployed weight. This recovers stranded capacity: taking the stronger realization per teacher, +2.36/+2.71/+10.45 Avg9 over matched-budget plain-LRC baselines across three teachers (Llama3.2-3B, Llama3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-3B), with the largest gain on the widest teacher (Qwen), where it reaches the original recipe's approx. 20B-token accuracy at 10B tokens (2x token efficiency); there the strictly same-lineage arm still recovers +6.39, the fully controlled figure. Controls strongly support attributing the gain to the enlarged reachable set, rather than to added parameters or the recipe. From approx. 10B distillation tokens plus a short SFT, a half-parameter 1.5B student matches its approx. 9T-token teacher's 9-task macro-average, within evaluation noise and with a residual MMLU deficit, and a 2.7B student beats Meta's own official compression of Llama3.1-8B at ~900x fewer compression tokens (a token count under unmatched recipes, not a compute claim). All results are from single-seed runs on the LRC backbone.

title: VTOS: Learning to Orchestrate Vision Tools by Co-Searching Solutions and Observers
abstract: Vision foundation tools such as open-vocabulary detectors, segmentation models, and post-processing operators are powerful building blocks for computer vision, but their effectiveness depends heavily on how they are orchestrated: which tools are used, in what order, with what parameters, and under what visual conditions. Existing visual-programming agents typically generate a fixed solution pipeline, making them brittle under dense objects, occlusion, small targets, and domain shift. We introduce VTOS (Vision Tools Orchestration Search), a framework for adaptive visual tool orchestration through joint solution-observer search. VTOS co-searches executable solution programs that compose vision tools such as Grounding DINO, SAM, NMS, and slice-and-detect, together with observer programs that diagnose candidate solutions, identify failure modes, and generate actionable feedback. These observations are accumulated in a shared VisionThoughts knowledge base to guide subsequent search. We evaluate VTOS through two case studies: dense object counting on LVIS-Count and zero-shot plant-disease segmentation on PlantSeg-OOD, which stress different orchestration challenges including threshold calibration, NMS, slicing, mask refinement, and domain generalization. Across both tasks, VTOS outperforms static tool pipelines and agentic visual-programming baselines, specifically in complex settings such as dense, occluded scenes and out-of-distribution segmentation where static pipelines leave measurable headroom, rather than in standard tasks where a single well-calibrated tool already approaches its ceiling.

title: FailSAE: Towards Interpretable Failure Prediction for Vision-Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs), such as CLIP, have achieved strong performance across multimodal tasks by aligning visual and textual representations in a shared embedding space. As VLMs are increasingly used for high-stakes domains, failure prediction becomes critical for risk-aware deployment and human intervention. Existing failure prediction methods typically rely on confidence scores or auxiliary classifiers. Although these methods are effective on predicting VLM failures, they provide limited interpretability. In this work, we investigate the use of Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) for interpretable failure prediction in VLMs. We formulate failure prediction as a classification task over sparse SAE latent activations and introduce a three-stage failure-aware training pipeline that encourages the learned latent directions to remain interpretable while becoming more informative for failure prediction. Our experiments show that the resulting framework outperforms the evaluated baselines in failure prediction. Further analysis suggests that failure-aware training encourages SAE latent directions to capture more class-specific concepts. We also use the SAE to provide a concept-level analysis of how model representations change during failures, revealing a shift from class-specific concepts toward more ambiguous or style-related concepts. Finally, we explore how the learned SAE latent directions can support runtime failure recovery.

title: A Tri-Agent Framework for Evaluating and Aligning Question Clarification Capabilities of Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in interactive systems where understanding user intent precisely is paramount. A key capability for such systems is effective question clarification, especially when user queries are ambiguous or underspecified. This paper introduces a novel tri-agent framework for the robust evaluation of an LLM's ability to engage in clarifying dialogue. Our framework comprises three distinct LLM-based agents: (1) a Question Clarifying Agent (QCA), the system under evaluation, tasked with identifying ambiguities and posing clarifying questions; (2) a Respondent Agent (RA), designed to simulate human user responses, potentially including irrelevant or challenging replies; and (3) an Evaluator Agent (EA), an LLM-as-a-judge, which assesses the quality of the dialogue based on a comprehensive set of metrics. We detail a methodology for synthetic data generation in the supply chain domain as an example. We propose metrics evaluating ambiguity handling, question quality, dialogue efficiency, language appropriateness, and final intent alignment. We also briefly discuss the validation of the EA against human judgments. This work provides a structured approach to benchmark, validate, and improve the clarification capabilities of conversational LLM applications.

title: Energy Field Optimization via Quantum Field Simulation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel energy field optimization method based on quantum field simulation. Traditional methods often rely on static models, limiting the accuracy of physical simulations and predictions. This approach leverages the dynamic nature of quantum fields to accurately model complex physical phenomena, offering a significant advancement in computational power and predictive capability. The core mechanism involves simulating energy field changes within a quantum framework, iteratively refining the energy field to achieve optimal results. This methodology demonstrates improved precision and efficiency in simulating and predicting a range of physical systems, particularly in molecular dynamics and materials science.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to matrix aggregation, termed Non-Linear Matrix Self-Adaptive Aggregation Learning (NLMAAL), designed to enhance the generalization capabilities of machine learning models. Traditional aggregation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the model's ability to adapt to complex data patterns. NLMAAL dynamically adjusts aggregation weights based on the data's inherent non-linear relationships, enabling the model to automatically learn and optimize its representation. The paper details the core mechanisms of the method, including a dynamic weighting scheme and a novel optimization strategy to mitigate the limitations of fixed parameter approaches. We demonstrate the effectiveness of NLMAAL through extensive experimentation on several benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in model performance and robustness.

title: Probability Field Simulation for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic field simulation approach designed to enhance quantum computing by leveraging its inherent advantages and utilizing parallel computation to accelerate algorithm validation and optimization. Traditional quantum computing demands extreme precision, while probability field simulation offers a pathway to significantly reduced computational complexity. The core mechanism involves approximating quantum computation through a probabilistic framework, effectively utilizing parallel computation to expedite the verification and refinement of quantum algorithms. This work presents a framework for efficient quantum algorithm design and validation, demonstrating the potential for significantly improved computational performance. The paper provides a detailed explanation of the methodology, showcasing its benefits and limitations.

title: Title: Bayesian Constraint Optimization for Quantum Field Theory
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian Constraint Optimization (BCO) to quantum field theory simulations. Traditional parameter tuning methods often rely on trial-and-error, which can be computationally expensive and may not accurately capture the underlying physics. We propose a novel Bayesian framework leveraging a dynamically adjusted Bayesian network to intelligently prioritize energy stability and coherence – key aspects of quantum field theory. The core mechanism involves a 'Adaptive Bayesian Network' that learns the field's dynamics through observation, effectively addressing the inherent uncertainty in complex quantum systems. This approach aims to provide more accurate simulations and accelerate optimization processes compared to conventional methods. The paper details the architecture of the Bayesian network, the learning process, and the resulting performance improvements, demonstrating the efficacy of the BCO framework in simulating fundamental quantum phenomena. The research focuses on a specific example of simulating the Klein-Gordon field, providing a concrete illustration of the methodology's potential.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Deep Learning Hyperparameters via Tensor Networks
abstract: Optimizing hyperparameters in deep learning models remains a significant bottleneck in the development and deployment of effective neural networks. Traditional methods, such as grid search and random search, often struggle with the exponentially growing search space, leading to substantial computational costs and limited exploration of potentially optimal configurations. This paper proposes a novel approach to deep learning hyperparameter optimization that leverages the principles of quantum-inspired optimization, specifically employing tensor network methods, notably Matrix Product States (MPS), to efficiently approximate the complex optimization landscape. Our method utilizes quantum-inspired sampling techniques to guide the exploration, effectively mimicking the probabilistic nature of quantum measurements. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential advantages of this approach through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework. The core of our method lies in representing the hyperparameter space as a tensor network, allowing for efficient calculations of the objective function (e.g., validation loss) without exhaustively evaluating every possible combination. This significantly reduces the computational burden compared to conventional methods. The paper outlines a detailed algorithm and discusses key considerations for implementation, including tensor network construction, sampling strategies, and convergence criteria. We propose a framework for iteratively refining the tensor network representation based on observed validation performance, ultimately converging towards a high-performing hyperparameter configuration. The theoretical underpinning draws upon concepts from quantum mechanics, particularly the idea of measurement and probability distribution, to drive the optimization process. We believe this quantum-inspired approach offers a promising avenue for accelerating deep learning hyperparameter tuning and achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding via Relational Diffusion
abstract: Graph embeddings have emerged as a powerful technique for representing graphs in a continuous vector space, facilitating downstream tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and graph clustering. However, conventional graph embedding methods often treat graph relationships as static, failing to capture the dynamic evolution of these relationships over time. This paper introduces a novel approach, Temporal Graph Embedding via Relational Diffusion, which addresses this limitation by explicitly modeling the temporal dynamics of graph relationships. We leverage a recurrent neural network (RNN) to learn a "diffusion" process across the graph, where node states are iteratively updated based on the states of their neighbors, weighted by learned relational similarity. This process generates a temporal graph embedding where each node is represented by its evolving state vector. The core of our method lies in the integration of relational information within the RNN's recurrent computations, allowing the model to adapt to changes in the graph's structure over time. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline that our approach provides a more nuanced representation of graph data, potentially leading to significant improvements in graph-related tasks that require understanding temporal dependencies. This work lays the foundation for future research exploring more sophisticated temporal graph embedding techniques.

title: 基于量子纠缠的非局域性建模与优化
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a potentially transformative approach to modeling and optimization. This paper explores the application of entanglement principles to construct a novel non-local modeling framework, focusing on leveraging entanglement's inherent properties to enhance optimization processes. We propose a mechanism that translates complex problems into entangled states, enabling efficient transformation and potentially unlocking novel solutions. The core claim posits that this framework significantly improves the performance of optimization algorithms, particularly in scenarios where classical methods struggle. This work presents a conceptual foundation for future research and development in leveraging entanglement for advanced optimization techniques.

title: Differential Privacy for Training Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for learning representations from graph-structured data, finding applications in diverse domains like social network analysis, drug discovery, and recommendation systems. However, training GNNs often requires access to sensitive data, raising significant privacy concerns. This work introduces a novel differential privacy mechanism specifically designed for training GNNs. Our approach adds calibrated noise to the gradients during the training process, providing a quantifiable level of privacy protection while maintaining the network's ability to learn effective graph representations. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and conceptual design. The core claim of this work is to develop a differential privacy mechanism that protects the privacy of the training data while still allowing graph neural networks to learn effective representations. The core mechanism involves adding noise to the gradients during the training process, carefully calibrating the noise level to balance privacy and utility. This addresses the privacy challenges of training GNNs.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology for Data Compression – Quantum-Inspired Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive topology in data compression, inspired by the principles of quantum mechanics, to achieve significantly higher compression rates than conventional methods. Traditional compression algorithms rely on static mapping and iterative compression. We propose a novel approach that dynamically adjusts the topology of data structures, identifying and exploiting patterns that maximize information density, leveraging quantum-inspired algorithms to achieve this optimization. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum algorithms to subtly modify the underlying structure of data representations, leading to a more efficient compression process. The paper details the theoretical framework for this adaptive topology, explores the implementation challenges, and presents initial results demonstrating the potential for substantial compression gains. We argue that this approach represents a significant step toward quantum-inspired data compression, offering a pathway to unprecedented compression efficiency.

title: Self-Healing Neural Networks via Causal Bayesian Network-Based Diagnostics
abstract: Neural networks have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, yet their inherent fragility and susceptibility to unexpected failures remain a significant challenge. Traditional approaches to neural network failure diagnosis often rely on reactive methods – detecting and correcting errors after they occur. This paper proposes a novel approach to self-healing neural networks by integrating a causal Bayesian network (CBN) to monitor the network's internal state and perform diagnostics. The core idea is to leverage causal relationships between network parameters and observed performance degradation to proactively identify and address potential issues. This approach allows for a deeper understanding of the network's dynamics and enables targeted interventions. Specifically, we develop a framework where the CBN acts as a diagnostic tool, continuously learning and updating its understanding of the network's causal structure. The system identifies causal relationships, enabling the network to adapt its parameters or trigger corrective actions to mitigate performance degradation. This research provides a framework for building more robust and self-healing neural networks.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Learning Symbolic Representations
abstract: This paper explores the application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to the learning of symbolic representations from data. Traditional machine learning approaches often rely on numerical representations, which can struggle to capture the underlying structure and relationships within complex datasets. We propose a novel framework where a GAN is trained to generate symbolic representations – such as logical formulas or mathematical expressions – directly from data. The core of this approach lies in a discriminator that assesses the "symbolic quality" of the generated representations, providing a feedback signal to the generator. This process encourages the generator to produce representations that are not only plausible but also reflect the inherent structure of the data. We argue that this method represents a significant step towards enabling machines to reason and understand concepts in a manner more akin to human cognition. The potential applications span diverse fields, including knowledge representation, automated reasoning, and formal verification.

title: Adaptive Graph Neural Networks with Dynamic Attention Mechanisms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Adaptive Graph Neural Network (AGNN) architecture designed to address the limitations of traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in dynamic environments. Traditional GNNs typically rely on fixed graph structures and static attention weights, which can lead to suboptimal performance when graphs evolve over time or when node attributes change. The proposed AGNN incorporates dynamic attention mechanisms that adapt to these changes, improving learning efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that monitors graph structure modifications and node attribute updates, dynamically adjusting the attention weights to prioritize relevant neighbors and features. This approach enables the AGNN to effectively capture temporal dependencies and adapt to varying graph topologies, ultimately leading to enhanced performance in tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and graph classification. The experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the AGNN compared to standard GNNs, highlighting the benefits of dynamic adaptation.

title: Full Bayesian Analysis of ARX Models Under Scale-Mixtures of Normal Errors: An Application to Solar Radiation in Najran, Saudi Arabia
abstract: Autoregressive models with exogenous variables (ARX) constitute a fundamental family of time series tools with broad applicability across engineering, environmental science, and finance. A persistent limitation of standard Bayesian treatments is the Gaussian error assumption, which frequently proves inadequate when dealing with real data displaying heavy tails or occasional extreme observations. To overcome this shortcoming, the present paper develops a complete Bayesian inferential framework for ARX models under the scale-mixtures of normal (SMN) error distribution, integrating model identification, parameter estimation, and multi-step-ahead prediction within a unified scheme. A stochastic search variable selection (SSVS) procedure is adapted to perform simultaneous selection of the autoregressive order and the active exogenous regressors by assigning binary latent indicators to each candidate coefficient. Mixture-of-normals priors are specified for the dynamic and exogenous coefficients and an inverse-gamma prior for the error scale, while Bernoulli priors govern the latent selection indicators. These choices yield tractable full conditional posterior distributions: multivariate normal for the complete coefficient vector, inverse-gamma for the scale, and Bernoulli for the indicators. The conditional predictive distribution of future observations is also multivariate normal. For SMN-specific mixing parameters whose conditionals lack standard forms, Metropolis–Hastings steps are embedded within the Gibbs sampler. An extensive simulation study evaluates recovery accuracy across three SMN distributions and several ARX configurations. The methodology is then applied to the forecasting of daily global horizontal irradiance (GHI) in Najran, southwestern Saudi Arabia, using clear-sky GHI as an exogenous covariate, demonstrating the practical value of the proposed framework in a renewable energy context.

title: pcNN-SN: a physics-enhanced predictor-corrector neural network algorithm coupled with the discrete ordinates method for neutron transport equations
abstract: Super-resolution machine learning methods hold promise for addressing the high computational costs associated with high-dimensional features in traditional transport simulations. This paper proposes a physics-enhanced neural network coupling algorithm for discrete ordinates (SN) transport calculations. Based on high- and low-accuracy data, we develop a predictor-corrector neural network (pcNN) to predict correction factors for coarse-grid solutions. Based on transport equations, local physical features containing subgrid-scale information are selected as network inputs. Dimensionless transformation of physical quantities reduces the input space dimensionality and narrows parameter distributions, facilitating network training. Physical constraints are incorporated into the network model, and the corrected solution retains its original conservation properties. pcNN and SN transport sweeps are internally coupled, and numerical solutions are corrected online. Numerical results demonstrate that this algorithm can effectively improve coarse-grid solutions to achieve a level of accuracy comparable to that of fine-grid results. The physics-based network design enables the model to demonstrate a certain degree of reusability under different computational conditions. Compared to mesh refinement, the pcNN-SN algorithm reduces the computation time for the three-dimensional test problem by more than 60%.

title: Sparse concept attribution for histomorphological hypothesis generation from whole-slide classifiers
abstract: Histology images contain rich morphological information and can provide insights into pathological processes. However, deriving hypotheses relating morphological phenotypes to clinical attributes is bottlenecked by a manual image interpretation step. Here, we demonstrate that this process can be automated through interpretable deep learning. We present SCOPE, a method to interpret slide-level classifiers by combining pathology-specific vision--language models with sparse concept attribution onto a generalist histomorphological concept bank. To measure whether such explanations recover known morphology, we introduce MorphoRecoveryBench, a benchmark of seven tasks with pathologist-curated reference descriptions. On this benchmark, dense concept attribution is indistinguishable from a random baseline, whereas sparse attribution recovers substantial known morphology; decomposing the pooled slide embedding reaches similar explanation correctness at a fraction of the computational cost. Post-hoc interpretation of whole-slide classifiers can thus generate morphological hypotheses at scale, for expert validation.

title: The Import Tax: A Longitudinal Measurement of Startup Cost in the Python Ecosystem
abstract: Companion dataset to "The Import Tax: A Longitudinal Measurement of Startup Cost in the Python Ecosystem" (revised version under review at Software: Practice and Experience; preprint arXiv:2609.02753). It contains every measurement used in the paper, the -X importtime traces, the measurement harness, and the analysis scripts that regenerate every number and figure. What was measured: the import time of the 500 most-downloaded PyPI packages, every quarterly release since 2021Q3, on CPython 3.9 to 3.14 (python-build-standalone builds), on two platforms (Apple M5 / macOS and Intel Xeon E5-2665 / Linux): 33,408 cells per platform, plus the release histories of 65 distributions that live beneath shared namespaces, and the targeted experiments of the revision (dependency-resolution drift under sweep-date and release-era dependencies, hidden submodule cost with usage weighting, cold-start decomposition including a macOS first-load experiment, and the global lazy mode of CPython 3.15). Files: import-tax-dataset.tar.gz holds README.md (data dictionary and provenance), raw/ (all measurement records as gzipped JSONL), analysis-view/ (the matrix with unit-of-analysis annotations), code/ (harness, analysis and Slurm scripts) and SHA256SUMS; the -X importtime traces are nine separate files traces- .tar.gz (place them under import-tax-dataset/traces/ as .tar.gz). title: InceptionGS: Generative Bootstrapping for Large-Scale Gaussian Splatting under Unstructured View Sampling
abstract: Achieving truly immersive large-scale scene digitization necessitates consistent and visually pleasing rendering across all possible viewing perspectives. However, collecting multi-view images covering every fine detail of a large-scale scene is prohibitive due to scene complexity, capture cost, negligence, or accessibility constraints. As a result, the sampled views tend to be highly unstructured -- the majority of the scene is well covered yet certain regions inevitably lack sufficient observations. Existing reconstruction based methods are vulnerable to view scarcity while generation based approaches suffer from generalization, controllability, and 3D consistency issues. To address this challenge, we propose InceptionGS, which bootstraps Gaussian splatting by subtly balancing reconstruction and generation. Starting from an initial Gaussian splatting, InceptionGS reasonably rethinks and repairs problematic regions caused by view scarcity while preserving the quality elsewhere, by softly incorporating scene- and view-adaptive generative priors. Extensive experiments on real-world large-scale scenes demonstrate the superiority and broad applicability of our approach in handling unstructured imagery and boosting high-fidelity Gaussian splatting. Please refer to the supplementary video for better visual demonstrations.

title: PhoenixNest-Video: Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Agent Framework for Automated Video Interview Assessment
abstract: Interview assessment requires per-criterion judgments grounded in behavioral evidence, yet surging applicant volumes have made human-only evaluation costly and inconsistent, while existing AI approaches yield opaque scores without traceable rationale. We introduce PhoenixNest-Video, an evidence-grounded multimodal agent framework for automated video interview assessment. It builds a semantic video graph as structured working memory, performs rubric-conditioned retrieval with cross-modal verification across visual, audio, and textual streams, and produces per-criterion scores anchored to the candidate's materials. A Scorer trained via Rubrics-based Reinforcement Learning with dual rewards for rubric alignment and score-level differentiation internalizes the discriminative structure of multi-level rubrics. PhoenixNest-Video attains 91.50\% grade-level accuracy on VInterview-2025, outperforming substantially larger proprietary models. A compact, rubric-grounded agent therefore scores candidates in closer agreement with an expert panel than direct prompting of much larger models, and exposes the evidence behind each score for human review.

title: InstEditSeg: Instruction-Driven Image Editing for Polyp and Skin Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Accurate segmentation of polyps and skin lesions is pivotal for clinical diagnosis, yet existing methods struggle with low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, and cross-domain distribution discrepancies. Discriminative networks and most diffusion-based segmentation approaches predict standalone binary masks, leaving the visual priors of large-scale pretrained generative models largely unexploited. We propose InstEditSeg, a unified generative framework that reformulates medical segmentation as an instruction-driven image editing problem. Instead of emitting a mask, the model renders a color-coded overlay on the original image, conditioned on a textual instruction, so that the edited output aligns with the natural image distribution learned by latent diffusion models and mitigates the domain gap between natural and medical imagery. To recover fine anatomical structures, we introduce DINOv3 as an auxiliary visual encoder and a DINO Feature Guidance Block that builds a multi-scale feature pyramid. The pyramid is fused into the diffusion U-Net by channel concatenation and zero-initialized convolution so that hierarchical discriminative priors can be injected without perturbing the pretrained weights. A dual-branch classifier-free guidance strategy requiring only two forward passes per denoising step reduces inference cost. On polyp and skin lesion benchmarks the framework achieves accuracy competitive with strong discriminative baselines, and it further demonstrates concrete advantages of the generative formulation: notably better cross-domain generalization on unseen data, more complete multi-lesion segmentation, instruction-conditioned task control, and sampling flexibility. We also analyze the strengths and limitations of the paradigm, including its color sensitivity and unsupported attribute-conditioned selection. Code is available at: https://github.com/wincharm001/InstEditSeg.

title: EComAgentBench: Benchmarking Shopping Agents on Long-Horizon Tasks with Distributed Hidden Intent
abstract: As LLM-based shopping agents enter production, existing benchmarks fail to capture how a shopper's requirements arrive: stated implicitly in the query, recorded in a profile, or revealed only when the right question is asked. Benchmarks that expose full intent upfront and grade only the final choice can neither pose this long-horizon challenge nor explain which requirement an agent missed. To address this gap, we introduce EComAgentBench, a benchmark of 662 tasks grounded in real Amazon products and reviews. Each task scatters these requirements across a visible query, a tool-gated profile, and scripted clarification; an agent must uncover hidden intent, verify candidates against attributes and review evidence, and commit to a single product within 100 tool calls. Moreover, typed, source-tagged rubrics grade every task, attributing each failure to a requirement and its source. Construction is automated yet reliable, with every answer fixed in code before any text is generated and every sample validated. Our evaluation of seven models reveals that even the strongest attains only 57.1% overall accuracy, and rubric satisfaction degrades from visible to hidden sources. Overall, we believe EComAgentBench will serve as a reproducible foundation for moving shopping agents from single-query search toward dependable assistance over long horizons.

title: Poisoning Attacks on the PGM-index
abstract: The PGM-index (Ferragina and Vinciguerra, VLDB'20) is one of the most practical learned indexes, owing to its theoretical elegance and consistently strong empirical performance. It is built on optimal piecewise linear approximations (PLAs) that minimize the number of segments. In this paper, we ask how sensitive this optimal PLA itself is to poisoning attacks. We propose PGM-attack, an efficient poisoning attack that sequentially inserts adversarial keys to inflate the resulting number of segments, and we develop a method for deriving theoretical upper bounds on the number of segments attainable under arbitrary insertions. Our experiments show that poisoning only 10% of the keys allows PGM-attack to increase the segment count by up to 120x. On every evaluated instance, our instance-dependent upper bound is at most 1.92x the segment count attained by PGM-attack, certifying that PGM-attack achieves at least 52% of the optimum. This increase in the number of segments enlarges the PGM-index by up to 120x. Moreover, the attack also transfers to other learned indexes, substantially inflating the index size of PLA-based ones in particular. Our results reveal that, despite the optimality of its PLAs, the PGM-index has an intrinsic vulnerability rooted in its optimization objective, motivating robustness-aware objective design for future learned indexes. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/atsukisato/pgm-attack.

title: EmoStance: Response-Side Affective-Orientation Control for Empathetic Response Generation via Emoji Weak Supervision
abstract: Empathetic response generation requires models to decide not only what to say, but also how to respond to the previous speaker's affective situation. We formulate this as response-side affective-orientation control and use multi-annotator emoji distributions as weak affective--attitudinal evidence, rather than as output symbols or gold labels, to induce a latent control space that operationally approximates listener stance. We construct EmojiDialogue, an utterance-level extension of EmpatheticDialogues with emoji votes and confidence scores, and propose EmoStance, which models source-side affective expression, predicts a soft response-side orientation from dialogue context and speaker roles, and steers a frozen instruction-tuned LLM through continuous prefix embeddings. In blind pairwise evaluation with 20 annotators and 800 judgments, EmoStance achieves a 62.2% decisive win rate, with the clearest gains in contextual specificity and perceived responsiveness, while remaining complementary to external-knowledge methods. Code, annotation metadata, and reconstruction scripts are available in our GitHub repository: https://github.com/18277390221/EmoStance.

title: Measurement-Driven Sub-Network Selection for On-Premise Retrieval-Augmented Factory Agents
abstract: On-premise assistants can give factory workers conversational access to machine documentation, but models capable of the task rarely fit shop-floor hardware. We show that after structural compression and retrieval-grounded adaptation, model size is no longer a reliable predictor of adapted answer quality: general capability falls almost linearly with parameter count, while judged retrieval-augmented answer quality does not. We therefore treat deployment as a post-adaptation selection problem, committing one sub-network per device on judged answer quality and measured on-device throughput under a configurable general-capability floor and memory budget; rules that optimize size, speed, or quality alone each give up capability or throughput. A weight-shared supernetwork trained with sandwich-style in-place distillation keeps this selection inexpensive. In a manufacturing-manual case study, extraction costs 13.7 percent of the unpruned model's judged quality and retrieval-grounded distillation returns it to within 4.6 percent, recovering two thirds of the loss, and the same assistant runs across three heterogeneous edge tiers at 1.3 to 5 watts standby.

title: Privacy-Preserving Topology-Guided Safety for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems via Federated Graph Learning
abstract: Topology-guided safeguards for LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) train a GNN over the inter-agent communication graph to localize risky agents and intervene on the topology---but they assume one operator can pool all labeled traces. Across organizations that assumption breaks: episodes contain private prompts, tool outputs, and proprietary workflows, and no silo alone sees the full attack distribution. We cast privacy-preserving MAS safeguarding as graph federated learning and instantiate FGLGuard: each operator fits an edge-featured graph attention detector on its own judge-labeled episode graphs and shares only model updates. The method couples a proximal local objective for non-IID clients, domain-balanced aggregation, over-refusal-constrained threshold calibration, corroborated upstream scoring, and a guarded rewrite for blocked answers. Federation is not optional: off-the-shelf transfer collapses under distribution shift (AUROC 0.51 to 0.70 only after in-domain retraining), so a deployable guard must adapt on each site's private traces. On Agent-SafetyBench, R-Judge, and AgentDojo, federated FGLGuard exceeds the in-domain centralized ceiling on all three benchmarks without pooling any data---where unsupervised anomaly guards and local-only training fail. One guard federated across four different-domain operators comes within 0.03 AUROC of multi-domain centralization, while any single-domain guard collapses on the others. Live FGLGuard cuts AgentDojo's ground-truth attack-success rate by 43% at near-unguarded utility, zero API cost, and negligible capability loss.

title: 基于量子自旋的动态几何变形与量子信息编码
abstract: This paper explores the potential of harnessing quantum spin for dynamic geometric reshaping and quantum information encoding. Quantum spin offers a unique property – self-similarity – which promises to revolutionize quantum device design and information processing. We introduce a novel algorithm predicated on this property, utilizing iterative optimization to construct complex geometric structures within quantum systems. This structure, in turn, facilitates adaptive encoding, allowing for optimal data manipulation. The core mechanism leverages the inherent correlation of spin states to dynamically adjust the geometry, resulting in enhanced device performance and robust quantum information. This approach offers a pathway towards more efficient and versatile quantum technologies. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of this methodology in optimizing quantum systems for specific applications.

title: 基于非线性几何变换的量子计算优化
abstract: Quantum computing offers unprecedented computational power, but realizing this potential requires sophisticated optimization techniques. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of quantum circuits, particularly when dealing with non-linear geometric transformations. This paper introduces a novel quantum computing optimization algorithm, "Nonlinear Geometry Transformation-Based Quantum Computing Optimization," designed to automatically adjust quantum computation parameters based on dynamic geometric transformations. The core mechanism leverages the unique properties of non-linear geometry to optimize quantum circuits, leading to improved efficiency and accuracy. This approach overcomes limitations of conventional methods, providing a framework for automated optimization of quantum algorithms across a diverse range of tasks. The proposed algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through a series of simulations, showcasing significant improvements in performance compared to existing optimization techniques.

title: Geometry Topology Adaptive Parameter Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for parameter optimization based on geometric topology, designed to address complex systems and enhance adaptability and stability. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting parameters within a geometric topology framework, leveraging the inherent properties of space to guide optimization towards optimal solutions. The research explores the potential of this approach to overcome traditional optimization challenges, particularly in systems requiring robust behavior and responsiveness to changing conditions. This work demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed method through illustrative examples and detailed analysis, highlighting its advantages in terms of adaptability and stability compared to conventional optimization techniques.

title: 基于自适应的概率分布优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic distribution optimization algorithm based on adaptive learning. Traditional approaches often rely on static parameters, limiting their effectiveness when data distribution shifts. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts probability distribution parameters through an adaptive learning process, resulting in enhanced predictive capability. We detail the core mechanism, emphasizing the use of a self-adjusting learning strategy that responds to changing data patterns. This approach overcomes the limitations of static optimization techniques, offering a more robust and flexible solution for probabilistic modeling. The algorithm's core claim centers on the ability to maintain high predictive performance under variable data conditions.

We present a framework for constructing these networks and demonstrate its effectiveness through experimental results on a dataset exhibiting high dimensionality. The core mechanism focuses on adaptive network construction, offering a solution to a long-standing challenge in machine learning.

title: Information Entropy as a Cognitive Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cognitive architecture based on information entropy. The core idea is that information entropy, traditionally used in information theory, can effectively model and simulate key aspects of human cognition, particularly those related to uncertainty, exploration, and learning. We argue that leveraging the principles of entropy increase can drive intelligent agents to autonomously adapt and learn, mirroring the inherent exploratory tendencies observed in human thought. This architecture moves beyond traditional symbolic approaches and probabilistic models by directly incorporating the concept of information uncertainty as a fundamental driver of intelligent behavior. The paper outlines the key components of this architecture, including a decision-making framework based on entropy minimization and maximization, and discusses its potential applications in various domains, such as robotics, artificial intelligence, and cognitive science. We explore the theoretical foundations underpinning this approach and present a conceptual framework for building intelligent systems that can effectively navigate and learn within complex, uncertain environments. The central contribution lies in providing a mathematically rigorous and computationally feasible framework for understanding and replicating cognitive processes using a metric deeply rooted in information theory.

title: Dimension Generalization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dimension generalization algorithm designed to automatically expand dimensions while leveraging a dimensionality generalization mechanism. Traditional dimension computation often relies on manual design, while our approach offers dynamic dimension expansion. The core of the algorithm is based on deep learning, which allows for automatic learning of dimension generalization models and prediction of relationships between different dimensions. This capability significantly enhances the model's ability to capture complex dependencies and improve overall performance. We present a framework where the algorithm learns a mapping between dimensions, allowing it to extrapolate relationships across the entire dimensionality space. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods by providing a flexible and adaptable system for dimension expansion, ultimately leading to more robust and expressive models.

title: Symbolic Regression with Neural-Symbolic Hybrid Architectures
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to symbolic regression leveraging a hybrid architecture combining neural networks and symbolic regression techniques. The core idea is to exploit the strengths of both paradigms: neural networks for robust feature extraction and symbolic regression for equation generation and optimization. A genetic algorithm is employed to iteratively refine and evolve the candidate equations produced by the symbolic regression engine. The system's architecture incorporates a neural network to learn data representations, a symbolic regression engine to propose mathematical expressions, and a genetic algorithm to drive the evolutionary process. We demonstrate the system's capability to automatically discover mathematical equations from datasets, achieving improved accuracy and interpretability compared to traditional methods. The key innovations lie in the seamless integration of these components and the use of a genetic algorithm for effective equation refinement. The system offers a promising solution for various applications requiring automated mathematical discovery, including scientific data analysis, engineering modeling, and pattern recognition.

title: Formal Verification of Decentralized Consensus Algorithms Using Process Algebra
abstract: Decentralized consensus algorithms form the bedrock of blockchain technology and distributed systems, ensuring agreement among participants despite potential failures or malicious attacks. However, verifying the correctness and robustness of these algorithms presents a significant challenge. This paper proposes a rigorous approach to formal verification using process algebra, specifically Communicating Sequential Processes (CSP) and Pi-calculus. We demonstrate how process algebra can be employed to model decentralized consensus protocols accurately, capturing the intricate interactions between nodes. Through formal specification and verification, we identify potential vulnerabilities and ensure that the protocols satisfy desired properties, such as liveness, safety, and fault tolerance. The core contribution lies in moving beyond simplistic assumptions and providing a mathematically sound framework for ensuring the reliability of decentralized consensus algorithms, a critical step toward widespread adoption and secure operation of these systems. The presented methods offer a pathway to enhance confidence in the design and implementation of consensus protocols, mitigating risks associated with decentralized environments.

title: Quantum Entanglement's Non-Classical Geometry Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity for computation. This paper explores the potential of leveraging entanglement to develop a novel non-classical geometry computation method. We propose a framework that utilizes entanglement to perform complex geometric transformations, offering a potential leap forward in numerical computation, particularly for high-dimensional geometric problems. The core mechanism centers on exploiting the correlated properties of entangled states to achieve intricate geometric operations without the limitations inherent in classical approaches. This work investigates the feasibility and potential benefits of this approach, highlighting its advantages in handling complex geometric structures and offering a promising pathway toward more efficient and powerful numerical calculations.

title: Neural Topology Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to deep learning, termed Neural Topology Learning, which leverages the underlying physical topology of neuronal networks to enhance both training efficiency and generalization performance. The core premise is that conventional deep learning methods often overlook crucial topological information – such as the spatial arrangement, connectivity patterns, and local interactions between neurons – that are fundamental to biological neural systems. We introduce an algorithmic framework designed to directly learn these topological features from data. This framework integrates learned topological representations into model architectures or training processes, leading to significant improvements in learning speed and model robustness. The proposed methodology addresses a critical gap in current deep learning research by shifting the focus from solely relying on connection weights to explicitly modeling and utilizing the more intrinsic topological properties of neural networks. The efficacy of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.
