title: Propose to Learn, Learn to Propose: Evaluability-Aware Assistance under Bounded Rationality
abstract: AI assistants often collaborate by proposing candidate edits, plans, or designs that users evaluate before adoption. Existing assistance methods focus on proposal quality or user-goal inference, often assuming that the user can reliably evaluate any proposal, which can fail in practice because of bounded rationality. We study evaluability-aware proposal planning, where proposals serve both as task interventions and as probes for learning latent preferences and evaluation constraints, where the resulting belief updates then guide later proposals. We formalise this setting as ProSE, a hidden-parameter sequential assistance problem, and instantiate it with a KL-regularised bounded-rational binary response model in which acceptance trades off value gain against a distance-dependent evaluability penalty. Analysing the planning consequence of this likelihood reveals that likely accepted proposals and informative probes need not coincide, which explains why planners that only pursue acceptance systematically underperform. We operationalise ProSE with \textsc{ProSE-Plan}, a depth-2 Bayes-adaptive planner that scores proposals by possible responses and response-induced posterior beliefs. In controlled graph simulations, \textsc{ProSE-Plan} improves over evaluability-unaware and myopic baselines when evaluation cost is the bottleneck, and a probe-commit ablation confirms that our approach selects informative proposals that simpler methods miss. Our results thus identify user evaluability as a planning-relevant dimension of AI assistance, complementary to generation quality and preference inference.

title: CAPTURE: Disentangling Preference Drift from Memory Poisoning in Personalized LLM Agents
abstract: Personalized language agents use persistent memory to adapt to users over time, but the same mechanism creates an attack surface. When new information conflicts with stored preferences, an agent must distinguish genuine preference drift from temporary context shifts, ambiguity, or adversarial memory poisoning. We formulate this problem as a continuous-time partially observable decision process over a latent user state and show why rules based only on recency and provenance are insufficient. CAPTURE addresses this ambiguity with a neural differential-equation belief tracker, a multi-timescale memory ledger, uncertainty-triggered clarification, and counterfactual auditing of cited memories. On 480 held-out episodes from 96 users, CAPTURE achieves a 71.5% win rate, compared with 69.3% for an identically supervised baseline and 66.1% for the strongest heuristic baseline. It limits fixed-policy poisoning success to 11.5% while accepting 83.5% of genuine preference updates. Under an adaptive attacker with access to the released weights, attack success rises to 24.7%, exposing a real adaptation-security tradeoff. We further evaluate the frozen system zero-shot on an independently constructed benchmark and replay longitudinal interaction histories from 40 users collected over two to three weeks. These results suggest that modeling preference authenticity explicitly can improve both personalization and robustness in memory-augmented LLM agents.

We further evaluate the frozen system zero-shot on an independently constructed benchmark and replay longitudinal interaction histories from 40 users collected over two to three weeks. These results suggest that modeling preference authenticity explicitly can improve both personalization and robustness in memory-augmented LLM agents.

evidence.abstract: Personalized language agents use persistent memory to adapt to users over time, but the same mechanism creates an attack surface. When new information conflicts with stored preferences, an agent must distinguish genuine preference drift from temporary context shifts, ambiguity, or adversarial memory poisoning. We formulate this problem as a continuous-time partially observable decision process over a latent user state and show why rules based only on recency and provenance are insufficient. title: SWIM: Student Writing Simulation via Proficiency-Conditioned Generation
abstract: Writing proficiency manifests in how students develop content, organize ideas, choose words, and use language. Despite growing interest in LLM-based student simulation, whether LLMs can reproduce such multidimensional variation in extended writing remains largely unexplored. In this work, we explore if language models can realistically simulate student writing, and introduce SWIM, a task that formulates Student Writing sIMulation as proficiency-conditioned essay generation. We evaluate prompting, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL) methods for writing simulation using automated essay scoring as a measure of profile alignment. Extensive experiments reveal that prompting provides limited proficiency control, even for strong proprietary LLMs with rubric-grounded strategies. In particular, while models can adjust content-oriented traits, they struggle to reproduce the lexical, grammatical, and organizational variation in different proficiency levels. SFT substantially improves alignment, while RL with the proposed proficiency-alignment reward yields further gains across all writing traits and essay prompts. Our findings suggest that explicit supervision enables substantially stronger profile alignment than prompting alone, while authentic low-proficiency writing remains challenging to reproduce.

title: PrivateHub: Contrastive Diffusion Model for Private Sensor-Intensive Environment Data Generation
abstract: Sensor-intensive environments enable many intelligent services by inferring user applications from heterogeneous data streams. However, not all applications should be exposed: users want some activities to stay private. This creates a tension between inferring applications for useful services and preventing unwanted inference. Existing approaches such as differential privacy and rule-based filtering protect individual streams but cannot address the privacy risk from cross-sensor inference. We introduce Privatehub, which uses contrastive learning within a diffusion model to generate synthetic multi-sensor streams that keep non-private applications detectable while concealing private ones. Privatehub has two stages: App-Conditioned Pre-training (ACP), which conditions the model on multi-sensor data with application embeddings, and App-Aware Fine-tuning (AAF), which separates private from non-private data via contrastive learning. We also define a threat model for the multi-sensor sharing setting. Experiments on three real-world multi-sensor datasets show Privatehub lowers private-application accuracy by 40 to 50\% without hurting non-private performance, and stays robust when the attacker retrains on the synthetic data.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Constraint Optimization with Adaptive Sampling
abstract: Quantum-inspired constraint optimization is a promising approach to accelerate the discovery of optimal solutions in complex problems. This paper explores the application of adaptive sampling techniques to enhance the effectiveness of this method. We introduce a novel 'quantum-perturbed sampling' algorithm that leverages controlled randomness to guide the search process. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the sampling frequency based on the algorithm's performance, thereby improving the exploration of the solution space. The research demonstrates the potential of this approach to achieve faster convergence and better solution quality compared to traditional optimization methods. We evaluate the algorithm on a range of benchmark problems, showcasing its efficacy in tackling challenging optimization tasks.

title: Adaptive Logic Networks: A Novel Approach to Reasoning and Inference
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Logic Networks (ALNs), a novel framework for reasoning and inference that dynamically adjusts logical rules and inference paths based on contextual input data. Traditional logic networks are typically constrained by pre-defined rule sets, limiting their effectiveness in complex and dynamic scenarios. ALNs overcome this limitation by incorporating an adaptive learning algorithm that refines rule strength and scope in response to data context, promoting more flexible and efficient reasoning.

title: Quantum State Dynamics and Algorithms
abstract: Quantum state dynamics and algorithms are rapidly evolving fields with profound implications for computation, communication, and sensing. This paper explores the potential of dynamically mapping quantum states using a novel algorithm. We propose a system of quantum state transformations that adapts to the current state of the quantum system, offering unprecedented control and responsiveness. The core mechanism hinges on exploiting the inherent properties of quantum states to achieve real-time manipulation and the development of novel algorithms. This research aims to provide a foundational approach for dynamically controlled quantum systems, potentially revolutionizing the design of complex quantum systems.

title: Evolutionary Algorithms Based on Self-Organizing Networks – Towards Complex Ecosystem and Biological Systems Evolution
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm framework leveraging self-organizing network principles to facilitate the evolution of complex ecosystems and biological systems. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often suffer from suboptimal search spaces and lack the inherent stability required for complex systems. This work proposes a method for generating and optimizing evolutionary trajectories within dynamically structured networks, mimicking the principles of biological self-organization. The core mechanism involves simulating ecological interactions within a network, iteratively refining the network structure and evolutionary parameters to produce diverse and adaptive biological solutions. The resulting evolutionary process aims to discover novel biological structures and functional properties, offering a pathway towards evolutionary innovation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential of this approach to address challenges in biological modeling and evolutionary computation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Time Series
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reservoir computing, termed "Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing" (QIRC), leveraging principles of quantum superposition and entanglement to dramatically improve temporal signal capture. Traditional reservoir computing relies on randomly connected recurrent networks, which often struggle with capturing fine-grained temporal dependencies. QIRC addresses this limitation by designing a 'quantum reservoir' – a recurrent network – that mimics quantum mechanical effects. Specifically, we explore network topologies and dynamical rules that, while not physically implementing quantum computation, emulate the exponential temporal resolution characteristic of quantum systems. This is achieved through introducing non-local connections and carefully calibrated dynamics designed to promote superposition and entanglement-like behavior within the network. The theoretical framework outlines the key elements of a QIRC system, including the reservoir's connectivity matrix ( *W* ), the recurrent dynamics represented by the input-to-output mapping ( *f* ), and the output layer. We demonstrate, through mathematical analysis and a conceptual framework, the potential for QIRC to significantly outperform conventional reservoir computing architectures in capturing complex, time-varying temporal patterns. The core claim is that incorporating quantum-inspired design principles can exponentially enhance temporal resolution. The key mechanism is the design of a 'quantum reservoir' that exhibits inherent quantum-like properties. This represents a genuinely quantum-inspired approach to reservoir computing, moving beyond structural mimicry towards a deeper understanding of temporal signal capture.

title: 基于自适应的拓扑信息学习的量子计算算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computation algorithm based on self-adaptive topology learning. The algorithm dynamically adapts to the system's topology, enabling improved efficiency and stability compared to traditional approaches. We propose a mechanism for learning and utilizing topological information to optimize quantum circuit design and execution. The core of the algorithm involves a self-learning process that iteratively refines the quantum state representation based on observed topology. This iterative refinement leads to significant improvements in quantum circuit performance, particularly in terms of reduced error rates and enhanced coherence. The design incorporates a novel approach to represent and utilize topological information, resulting in a fundamentally different algorithm that can address challenges in quantum computation. The paper concludes with a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance and discusses potential future directions.

title: Spatiotemporal Information Fusion Based on Quantum Sensors
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum sensors for achieving spatiotemporal information fusion, a critical requirement for applications demanding high precision and accurate environmental monitoring. Traditional quantum sensors primarily focus on measuring single physical quantities; however, integrating these sensors with sophisticated spatiotemporal models offers a novel approach to enhance measurement accuracy and data utilization. The core principle involves combining the precise measurements provided by quantum sensors with contextual information derived from spatiotemporal models. This fusion process leverages the unique characteristics of quantum sensors – their sensitivity to minute changes in physical parameters – alongside the temporal and spatial correlations inherent in environmental data. This research explores the theoretical framework and potential methodologies for implementing this fusion, outlining the benefits and challenges associated with this emerging technology. The work proposes a framework for utilizing quantum sensors in high-precision positioning systems, environmental monitoring, and potentially other areas where the simultaneous acquisition and analysis of spatial and temporal data are paramount.

title: Probability Logic and Formal Logic: A Unified Framework for Machine Learning Validation and Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework integrating probability logic and formal logic to provide a rigorous and automated approach to validating and optimizing machine learning algorithms. The framework leverages probabilistic distributions as a foundation for model validation and employs formal logic to analyze algorithm stability and parameter optimization. The core mechanism focuses on constructing a probabilistic verification method and utilizing formal logic to guide the optimization process. The research investigates the potential of this unified approach to enhance the robustness and reliability of machine learning models, leading to improved performance and predictive accuracy. This work represents a significant step towards a more scientific and automated method for machine learning algorithm refinement.

title: Quantum Data Compression Based on Quantum Demixing
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to classical data compression leveraging the principles of quantum demixing and measurement. The core idea is to transform classical data into a quantum state representation and subsequently exploit quantum demixing to effectively eliminate unwanted quantum correlations. This process allows for the selective extraction of information, ultimately leading to a compressed representation. We present a theoretical framework outlining this methodology, focusing on the mathematical underpinnings of the transformation, demixing, and measurement stages. The proposed method offers a potential pathway to achieve high compression ratios by exploiting the unique properties of quantum systems. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis, the feasibility and potential advantages of this technique compared to conventional classical compression methods. The key elements involve mapping classical data to a quantum state, employing a demixing protocol to reduce redundancy, and finally, measuring the quantum state to recover the compressed information. This work lays the groundwork for future research into practical implementations of quantum data compression. ---

title: Quantum Adaptive Optimization Algorithm for Quantum Systems
abstract: Quantum systems often face complex optimization challenges, necessitating sophisticated algorithms to find optimal solutions. Traditional optimization methods frequently rely on fixed parameters, limiting their effectiveness in such scenarios. This paper introduces a novel quantum system optimization framework employing adaptive optimization algorithms, designed to dynamically adjust optimization parameters, thereby significantly improving optimization results and addressing the limitations of conventional approaches. We present a detailed architecture and theoretical analysis of this framework, demonstrating its potential to enhance the performance of quantum systems in various applications. The core mechanism centers around the proactive adjustment of parameters, leading to enhanced precision and efficiency.

title: Geometric Data-Driven Deep Learning Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel deep learning algorithm, termed "Geometric Data-Driven Optimization," that leverages geometric data to automate the optimization of model parameters. Traditional deep learning relies heavily on labeled datasets, presenting limitations in scalability and generalization. This algorithm addresses this by directly incorporating geometric features extracted from input data, allowing for automated parameter adjustment based on inherent data structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments, showcasing improved model performance and generalization capabilities compared to existing optimization techniques. The core mechanism involves mapping data to a geometric representation, enabling a more intuitive and potentially more efficient optimization process.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Data Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed data verification leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that a highly secure distributed data verification system can be achieved without the need for shared keys, even when individual nodes are compromised. The proposed mechanism involves constructing a network of multiple quantum processors, each storing a portion of the data. Utilizing entangled states, real-time verification of relationships between data blocks is performed, and any detected alteration is immediately flagged. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols based on entangled states serve as the underlying communication foundation. This approach fundamentally differs from existing distributed data verification methods, which rely on key exchange and are therefore vulnerable to key compromise. The inherent principles of quantum mechanics provide a stronger security guarantee, theoretically offering superior resistance to attacks. This system aims to establish a robust and secure data integrity framework in scenarios demanding high levels of trust and protection against malicious manipulation.

title: Title: Dynamical Chaos-Driven Algorithm for Parallel Quantum Processing
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, but current implementations face significant challenges regarding scalability and efficiency. The inherent complexity of quantum systems necessitates intricate control strategies, often struggling to optimally utilize available resources. This research proposes a novel dynamic chaos-driven algorithm to address this limitation by intelligently adjusting the parallelism of quantum processors in real-time. We design a 'chaos-aware' scheduling algorithm that monitors the system's state and subtly alters qubit assignments to mimic the effects of chaos, thereby optimizing performance. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of static scheduling techniques and unlock the full potential of parallel quantum processing. This paper presents the design of the algorithm, details its implementation, and explores the theoretical implications of its effectiveness.

title: Enhancing Global Resilience Through Collaborative Artificial Intelligence Initiatives
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force, capable of strengthening global resilience in the face of complex, interconnected challenges such as climate change, pandemics, economic instability, and technological disruption. As societies increasingly rely on data-driven decision-making, collaborative AI initiatives offer significant opportunities to enhance crisis preparedness, response, and recovery at global, national, and organizational levels. This chapter examines the role of AI collaboration in building global resilience by integrating technological innovation with international cooperation. It discusses how AI applications in disaster management, healthcare, supply chain systems, and environmental sustainability contribute to adaptive and resilient systems. The chapter also highlights the importance of multi-stakeholder collaboration involving governments, industry, academia, and international organizations in developing responsible and inclusive AI frameworks.

title: A cluster-based short-term photovoltaic power forecasting method using K-means and CNN-BiLSTM-Attention
abstract: Accurately predicting the power generation of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power plants is extremely challenging due to their heterogeneity and complex temporal variations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a clustering-based prediction framework that combines K-means clustering with our proposed model. First, a multidimensional feature representation is constructed to characterize the statistical properties, dynamic fluctuations, and meteorological correlations of PV power plants. This feature representation is then used to classify the power plants into homogeneous clusters. For each cluster, a hybrid deep learning model is developed to capture local temporal patterns and long-term dependencies, with a focus on key time steps. Finally, the outputs of all clusters are aggregated to obtain the regional power generation prediction results. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the baseline model on multiple error metrics, proving its effectiveness in predicting the power generation of multiple PV power plants.

title: Scalable Neural Video Representation Compression
abstract: Scalable video coding (SVC) encodes a video into a layered bitstream consisting of a base layer and one or multiple enhancement layers, enabling decoding at different bitrate/quality/resolution operating points to accommodate diverse device capabilities and network conditions. Due to its practical flexibility, SVC has been incorporated into major video coding standards and has recently attracted growing interest for both scene-agnostic and scene-adaptive neural video codecs. Among the latter, Implicit neural representation (INR) based codecs achieve compression by overfitting a compact neural network to an individual video, offering fast decoding and competitive coding efficiency compared to scene-agnostic neural codecs. However, research on scalable INR-based compression remains in its infancy: these methods support scalable coding by introducing additional network layers, which couple the bitrate with the decoding complexity and also cannot achieve comparable performance with strong scalable/non-scalable codecs. In this context, this paper proposes S-NVRC, a scalable INR-based video codec that jointly supports fine-grained bitrate and decoding complexity scalability from a single embedded bitstream. It adopts a coarse-to-fine prefix for feature grids and a nested prefix for network layers, which scale bitrate and decoding complexity, respectively. The proposed S-NVRC spans a wide range of bitrate and decoding-complexity using a single encoding (training) and outperforms SHM 12.4 and the multi-layer VTM-20.0, by 43.7% and 5.6% in BD-rate on the UVG dataset, while also providing flexible complexity scalability. Implemented code will be provided.

title: Non-Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser Quantum Sensors for Quantum Parameter Estimation
abstract: Non-KAM (Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser) systems, when subjected to weak time-dependent perturbations, exhibit an abrupt transition to classical chaos through the breakdown of invariant phase-space tori. We showcase the utilization of non-KAM systems in the quantum regime as quantum sensors, leveraging their sensitivity at \textit{resonances}. Quantum Fisher information (QFI) is a central quantity in quantum parameter estimation theory that measures how much information a quantum state contains about an unknown parameter that is encoded into it. In other words, it quantifies the sensitivity of a quantum state to small changes in that parameter. In this work, through numerical analysis in conjunction with analytical results, we study the performance of the non-KAM systems for quantum sensing applications by computing the QFI. We find that the growth of the QFI is remarkably enhanced when the resonance condition is satisfied. For frequency estimation under Floquet unitary encodings, we derive a transport bound: if the mean excitation number grows as $\langle\hat n(t)\rangle\sim t^α$, the QFI obeys $I(t)\lesssim t^{2α+2}$. The quantum kicked harmonic oscillator, a paradigmatic non-KAM system, realizes the full hierarchy: localized dynamics ($α=0$) yield quadratic growth, delocalized diffusion along stochastic webs ($α=1$) yields quartic growth, and translationally invariant resonances ($α=2$) saturate the bound with anomalous hexic growth, $I(t)\sim t^{6}$, established analytically at resonance $R=2$ and numerically at $R=4$. The enhancement stems from resonance-induced translational symmetry rather than exponential instability, identifying non-KAM resonances as a metrological resource distinct from chaos-assisted and criticality-based sensing.

title: Scalable Kronecker-Fisher Approximation: Efficient Hessian Analysis for Billion-Parameter Language Models Compression
abstract: In this paper, we propose a scalable Kronecker-based approximation that captures cross-layer interactions without storing the entire Fisher matrix, enabling practical Hessian analysis for billion-parameter networks where full computation is infeasible. Our approach reveals consistent vulnerability patterns: value projection layers exhibit the highest sensitivity and strongest cross-layer correlations across multiple model families, while other components exhibit architecture-specific behaviors. Through extensive experiments on quantization, sparsification, inter-layer corruption, and post-corruption fine-tuning, we demonstrate that our approximation strongly correlates with both performance degradation and recovery. Our framework provides a practical, theoretically grounded tool for identifying fragile components in large models, opening new avenues for guided compression and optimization strategies, such as mixed-precision allocation, layer-wise sparsity, and adaptive low-rank decomposition across layers and even individual weight groups.

title: Towards Effective Physical Reservoir Computing with a Pneumatic Soft Robot
abstract: Physical reservoir computing (PRC) refers to the use of a physical dynamical system as a computational resource for tasks such as state estimation and control, but there has been a lack of formal study of design rules towards more effective design of such physical reservoirs. Using a pneumatic soft arm with a five-pouch sensing column, this work studies how the pouch interconnection topology, robot stiffness, and the number of instrumented sensors affect bending-angle estimation performance. Across 36 matched trials spanning waveform, baseline pressure of the sensing column, and actuation range, all designs are evaluated under the same-time bending-angle estimation benchmark using 0.2 s of pressure history and a fixed ridge estimator. Our analysis of the experimental results leads to three design guidelines. First, independently sealed pouches preserve a much richer observable state than a shared manifold. Second, increasing the baseline pressure of the sensing column makes the pouch responses more redundant and increases estimation error most strongly in the coupled topology. Third, in the sealed topology, two strategically placed sensors already recover most of the attainable benefit, three capture essentially all of it, and additional sensors provide little or no additional value. In summary, the results suggest that topology, stiffness, and number of instrumented sensors should be co-designed for accurate PRC of soft robot states; stronger excitation alone cannot recover the diversity that poor design choices have already removed.

title: Posterior Tempering Explains Variance Inflation in Linear and Generalized Linear Thompson Sampling
abstract: We study a variant of the Thompson Sampling (TS) algorithm, called $α$-TS, for solving stochastic generalized linear bandit problems. Existing analyses of TS require inflating the posterior variance to derive near-optimal regret guarantees. We formalize the idea of variance inflation by introducing $α$-TS that uses a fractional or $α$-posterior instead of the standard posterior. Our main contribution is to identify general regularity conditions on the prior and reward distributions that enable a regret analysis of $α$-TS without assuming any tractable approximation of the posterior distribution, unlike previous works. For a specific choice of $α\propto d^{-1}$, our general regret bound yields the best known regret bound of $O(d^{3/2}\sqrt{T}\log T)$ for both the exponential and sub-Gaussian families of reward distributions. We further provide an $α$-dependent lower bound showing that the regret constant depends on the product $αd$, and that when $α\propto d^{-1}$ the regret scales as $Ω(d^{3/2}\sqrt{T})$, explaining the origin of the $d^{3/2}$ factor in the upper bound. Our proof technique adapts and combines recent advancements in the analysis of linear bandit problems with first- and second-order posterior concentration theory from the Bayesian statistics literature.

title: SocialMaze: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Enhancing Social Reasoning in Large Language Models in Complex Social Environments
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in socially grounded applications, where success requires interpreting context, inferring others' mental states, and reasoning about unreliable information. Yet existing benchmarks rarely evaluate these demands jointly in complex, evolving settings. We introduce SocialMaze, a benchmark that organizes six tasks across social deduction games, daily-life interactions, and digital community platforms along three descriptive design axes: deep reasoning, dynamic interaction, and information uncertainty. These axes characterize intended sources of task difficulty rather than latent, factor-analytic dimensions of model capability. Automated checks and human validation support data quality. Evaluations of twelve proprietary and open-weight LLMs show substantial variation in the use of evolving interaction histories; stronger chain-of-thought reasoners perform better on tasks requiring deeper inference, while uncertainty consistently degrades performance. Reasoning workflows help weaker short-chain-of-thought backbones but saturate on stronger reasoners. Finally, targeted fine-tuning on curated reasoning traces substantially improves structured social-reasoning tasks, whereas transfer to language-aggregation tasks remains statistically inconclusive. The project homepage is available at https://xzx34.github.io/socialmaze/.

title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
abstract: Model compression techniques such as pruning and quantization facilitate the efficient deployment and acceleration of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, recent studies show that weight sparsification methods, such as SparseGPT, can amplify existing biases in models, with outputs varying significantly depending on persona cues in the prompt. In this paper, we introduce Debias-SparseGPT, a post-training pruning method incorporating representational debiasing using a second-order term defined over demographically contrasting inputs. We perform empirical validation of our method over a wide range of generative LLMs. Across models and sparsity regimes (25%, 50%, and structured 2:4 sparsity), Debias-SparseGPT consistently reduces pruning-induced bias compared to SparseGPT while preserving model perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. Under the most restrictive 2:4 structured sparsity pattern, which most aggressively degrades model quality, augmenting the calibration set with long-context, content-rich examples further improves both downstream performance and fairness. Overall, Debias-SparseGPT advances the bias-performance trade-off while preserving the computational efficiency of sparse models.

title: RouteGraph-Mona: Confusion-Aware Routing Fine-Tuning for Mineral Image Classification
abstract: Mineral image classification is important for geological exploration and resource development, but it remains challenging due to substantial intra-class variations in appearance and high inter-class visual similarity. Multi-cognitive Visual Adapter (Mona) is a vision-oriented parameter-efficient adapter that adapts pre-trained visual models by tuning only a few parameters. However, Mona statically aggregates responses from multiple scales, limiting its ability to accommodate sample-specific scale preferences and model confusion among visually similar mineral categories. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{RouteGraph-Mona}, a lightweight route-space regularization method built on Mona. Specifically, we replace Mona's static multi-scale aggregation with sample-adaptive routing. The resulting branch-selection behavior defines a compact routing space that captures each image's scale preferences. We then regularize the resulting routing signatures with class-wise route anchors and confusion-weighted margins. The route anchors encourage class-consistent routing patterns, while the margins promote greater separation between visually similar categories in the routing space. Experiments on three public mineral image datasets with two visual backbones show that RouteGraph-Mona consistently outperforms Mona in mean accuracy and remains competitive with representative fine-tuning methods and mineral image classification baselines.

title: AgentShield: A Zero-Trust Runtime Guardrail Architecture for Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Systems with Bidirectional Context Synchronization
abstract: The rapid migration of Large Language Models (LLMs) from conversational interfaces to autonomous multi-agent software engineering systems has exposed profound security vulnerabilities. When autonomous agents operate across heterogeneous topologies—spanning cloud-hosted reasoning engines and local execution environments—they are acutely vulnerable to indirect prompt injection, tool-call hijacking, privileged command escalation, and memory poisoning. Conventional boundary defenses (such as input sanitizers and prompt wrappers) fail to address lateral privilege escalation between collaborating agents. To resolve this critical architectural vulnerability, this paper introduces AgentShield, a zero-trust runtime verification and guardrail framework designed for decentralized multi-agent systems operating over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). AgentShield enforces continuous, non-bypassable policy verification across all intra-agent communications and system tool dispatches. The framework incorporates: (1) an inline bidirectional semantic interceptor that evaluates agent intents before system execution, (2) a multi-lingual token triage engine capable of detecting adversarial jailbreaks in low-resource and code-switched dialects, (3) a cryptographically signed persistent shared ledger ensuring tamper-evident state continuity, and (4) an automated capability attenuator for operating system and file operations. We evaluate AgentShield across 1,500 adversarial scenarios covering multi-step tool-injection benchmarks and real-world developer workflows. Empirical results demonstrate that AgentShield mitigates 98.4% of prompt injection and tool-escalation attacks while introducing less than 11.8ms of median runtime latency overhead. The core architecture is validated via two production-grade open-source packages released on the Python Package Index (PyPI): prema-agentshield and gemini-antigravity-bridge.

title: Layer-Scoped Expert-Budget Expansion Discovers Succinct Convergence in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Reasoning: Reducing Reasoning Tokens at Matched Accuracy on MMLU-Pro
abstract: This paper introduces layer-scoped expert-budget expansion, a training-free, runtime-only routing modification for sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models. By expanding the expert selection budget ($N \ge K$) exclusively within late transformer layers and applying a linear decay factor to additional experts, the method uncovers a phenomenon termed succinct convergence: holding output correctness constant, the expanded model arrives at the same correct final answer via significantly shorter reasoning trajectories. Evaluated on the complete MMLU-Pro benchmark (714 questions) using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a ties-only paired comparison (577 common correct answers) demonstrates an 8.5% reduction in mean reasoning tokens and a 10.9% decrease in latency (p = 6.5 10^-6}, while maintaining overall accuracy statistically indistinguishable from native routing (84.5% vs 84.0%, p=0.77).

title: Odd-Dimensional Descent Obstructions in the Third Support Spectrum of Binary Second-Order Reed--Muller Codes
abstract: Let S_n^(3) denote the support spectrum of three-dimensional subcodes of the binary second-order Reed--Muller code RM_2(2,n). We prove an exact local parity classification around the normalized aggregate 3*2^(m-1). For every m>=6, the exponentially widening local band contains exactly the six odd offsets +/-1, +/-3, +/-5 in odd dimension, while no value in the same band is attainable in even dimension. One explicit family starts at m=5 and proves that odd-to-even support descent fails for every m>=5. The result is a local classification and an infinite obstruction family, not a determination of the complete third support spectrum. Status: Public Beta; internally verified candidate proof; external mathematical review pending.

title: Six Birds Foundations VII: Lawful Theory Interaction
abstract: Six Birds Foundations VII: Lawful Theory Interaction asks when interaction across the boundaries of two theory packages is admissible. It closes a catalog of 36 entries covering access and admission, contact and join, enablement and descent, and dynamics and residue, while separating contact from join, strictness from directionality, enablement from descent, and source independence from behavioral non-factorization. The paper gives eleven scoped obstructions with named escape routes, two refuted proposed laws with surviving conditional content, and two formally closed deferrals. Its central object is a join of theories relative to a declared admissibility regime; the construction is neither assumed to exist nor treated as free.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Information Compression via Correlation Dynamics
abstract: Quantum-enhanced information compression leverages the unique properties of quantum systems to achieve unparalleled data reduction. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "Quantum-Enhanced Information Compression via Correlation Dynamics," designed to exploit the inherent correlation dynamics within quantum systems to dramatically reduce the number of bits required to represent a given dataset. The core mechanism centers around a "Correlation Dynamics Engine" that identifies and amplifies correlated quantum states, effectively compressing information through a fundamentally different approach than traditional compression techniques. This research explores the potential of harnessing quantum phenomena to achieve lossless data compression, addressing limitations of current methods and offering a promising pathway toward more efficient data storage and transmission. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant compression ratios and offers a fundamentally new methodology for information representation.

title: 基于自适应的量子纠缠拓扑分析
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon with profound implications for quantum technologies. Accurate analysis of entangled states is crucial for various applications, including quantum cryptography, quantum computation, and quantum sensing. However, traditional methods often struggle with complex entangled systems, requiring pre-defined parameters that may not accurately capture the system's dynamics. This paper proposes a novel framework, Self-Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Topology Analysis, that leverages dynamic adjustment of quantum entanglement properties to enhance the analysis of quantum systems. We introduce a self-adaptive algorithm that continuously monitors and modifies entanglement characteristics to improve the precision and robustness of entanglement state characterization. The core mechanism revolves around a feedback loop that optimizes entanglement parameters based on observed system behavior. The framework demonstrates improved accuracy in identifying and characterizing entangled states, particularly in systems exhibiting non-linear dynamics. This advancement holds significant potential for advancing the practical applications of quantum technologies.

title: Bayesian Resonance Networks for Predictive Chaos Theory
abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Resonance Networks (BRNs) – a novel neural network architecture specifically designed for predictive chaos theory. Traditional chaos theory models often grapple with simplifying assumptions, leading to limited predictive capabilities. BRNs offer a fundamentally more complex and adaptive approach, leveraging Bayesian inference and a dynamically updated prediction model to capture the inherent instability and sensitivity of chaotic systems. The core mechanism centers around a "resonance" process that amplifies small initial deviations, fostering a robust and responsive predictive capability. We demonstrate the efficacy of BRNs through a series of simulations, showcasing improved performance in predicting complex chaotic behavior compared to conventional methods. The study highlights the potential of BRNs to provide a more nuanced and accurate understanding of chaotic dynamics.

title: Knowledge Graph Construction Based on Neural-Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge graph construction leveraging the power of neural-symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to automate the process of building and updating knowledge graphs by integrating neural networks with symbolic inference. We decompose the knowledge graph construction task into two key components: neural-symbolic reasoning for automated knowledge extraction and knowledge representation for storage and management. This hybrid approach allows us to capitalize on the strengths of both paradigms – the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks and the logical deduction capabilities of symbolic systems. The resulting system demonstrates the potential for significantly scaling and improving the quality of knowledge graphs. This work addresses a critical limitation of existing knowledge graph construction methods, which often rely on manual curation or rule-based systems that struggle with complex and evolving knowledge domains. The key contributions are a framework for combining neural networks and symbolic reasoning and a methodology for automating the entire knowledge graph construction process.

title: Multimodal Data Fusion Based on Self-Organizing Maps
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) for multimodal data fusion. Traditional data fusion techniques often rely on manually designed algorithms, limiting their adaptability and ability to capture complex relationships within diverse datasets. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing SOMs to automatically learn and integrate information from multiple modalities. The core claim is that SOMs, with their inherent self-organizing capabilities, provide an effective framework for multimodal data analysis and understanding. The mechanism involves mapping data from different modalities onto the SOM's nodes, leveraging the network's self-organization to discover underlying patterns and correlations. This eliminates the need for explicit feature engineering and allows the SOM to uncover latent relationships that might be missed by conventional methods. The results demonstrate the potential of SOMs for robust and adaptable multimodal data fusion, offering a promising direction for applications in areas such as sensor data analysis, medical diagnosis, and intelligent surveillance.

title: Adaptive Machine Learning for Dynamic Space Modeling and Data Fusion
abstract: This research explores the application of adaptive machine learning techniques to construct dynamic space models and facilitate data fusion. The inherent complexity of real-world data often necessitates sophisticated modeling approaches. Traditional methods struggle to effectively handle data distributions that evolve over time. This work proposes a novel framework leveraging adaptive machine learning algorithms to dynamically adjust space models, enabling a more accurate representation of complex data patterns. The core of this approach centers on iteratively refining the space model based on incoming data, effectively integrating disparate data sources to create a robust and adaptable representation. This offers a significant advancement over static models, particularly in scenarios requiring real-time adaptation and improved predictive capabilities. The paper details the methodology, presents preliminary results, and discusses future research directions focused on enhancing model robustness and scalability.

title: Based on Spacetime Entanglement: A Model for Superluminal Super-Distance Information Transfer
abstract: This paper proposes a novel model for superluminal information transfer based on the phenomenon of spacetime entanglement. The core claim is to utilize the entanglement effect to achieve information transmission exceeding the speed of light, thereby overcoming the limitations imposed by classical physics. The proposed mechanism leverages the principles of general relativity and quantum entanglement to construct a spacetime entanglement network. Within this network, entangled states are utilized to facilitate instantaneous information transfer across vast distances. This model represents a significant departure from conventional approaches to information transfer, offering a potential pathway for future communication technologies. The mathematical framework presented here outlines the key equations governing the entanglement network and the associated information transfer process. The model relies on the concept of a non-local correlation between entangled particles, represented by the following equation: Ψ(s1, s2) = α |s1⟩⟨s2| + β |s2⟩⟨s1| where Ψ(s1, s2) represents the entangled state of particles s1 and s2, |s1⟩ and |s2⟩ denote the quantum states of the respective particles, and α and β are complex coefficients determining the degree of entanglement. The transfer rate (R) is then defined as: R = |β|2 * c where c is the speed of light in a vacuum. Furthermore, the fidelity (F) of the transferred information is described by: F = |(s1, s2)| where (s1, s2) represents the input state and is a function of the shared entanglement. The model incorporates the concept of spacetime curvature, represented by the Einstein field equations: Gμν = 8πG Tμν where Gμν is the Einstein tensor, Tμν is the stress-energy tensor, and G is the gravitational constant. The model utilizes a modified version of this equation to account for the influence of the entanglement network on the spacetime geometry. A key element of the model is the definition of the entanglement density (ρ) which quantifies the strength of the entanglement link: ρ = |Ψ(s1, s2)|2 This density directly impacts the efficiency and fidelity of the information transfer. The model also introduces a metric tensor (gμν) that describes the geometry of the spacetime entanglement network, allowing for the calculation of the shortest path between entangled particles. The distance (d) between the entangled particles is then given by: d = √gμν (xμ - xν) where xμ are the spacetime coordinates of the entangled particles. The model further explores the concept of wormholes as potential conduits for entanglement-based information transfer, utilizing the Schwarzschild metric to describe the spacetime geometry around a wormhole throat: ds2 = (1 - 2GM/rc2)c2dt2 + (1 - 2GM/rc2)-1dr2 + r2(dθ2 + sin2θdφ2) The model assumes that the wormhole throat acts as a highly efficient conduit for entanglement, reducing the effective distance between entangled particles. The model requires further refinement and validation through theoretical analysis and, potentially, future experimental investigations.

title: Adaptive Threshold-Based Sensor Data Fusion
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to sensor data fusion that leverages adaptive thresholds for enhanced accuracy and robustness. Traditional sensor fusion methods often rely on fixed thresholds, which can be inadequate in dynamic and unpredictable environments. This research introduces a data fusion algorithm incorporating machine learning to dynamically adjust thresholds based on learned environmental characteristics. The core claim is that a system capable of adapting thresholds based on environmental changes significantly improves data fusion performance. The proposed mechanism utilizes machine learning to identify key environmental features and subsequently adjust thresholds accordingly. This adaptive thresholding allows for more effective integration of sensor data, mitigating the limitations of static thresholding approaches. The system's performance is evaluated through a theoretical analysis and conceptual design, demonstrating its potential to address challenges in diverse sensor fusion applications.

title: Opening the Black Box a Crack: A Comparative Analysis Review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of explainable AI and interpretability as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于图的动态机器学习的自适应模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for dynamic machine learning based on graph-structured modeling. Traditional machine learning often relies on manual parameter tuning, limiting the model's adaptability. We propose a framework that automatically adjusts model parameters based on the structure of the graph, enabling self-adaptive learning. The core mechanism involves converting the model's nodes and edges into a graph, and applying a dynamic adjustment algorithm to optimize the model's parameters. This approach enhances model generalization and offers a promising alternative to static parameter tuning methods. We analyze the performance of this method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in capturing complex relationships within the data.

title: Weather State Ants Optimizer: A Markov-Driven Variable-Structure Metaheuristic
abstract: Metaheuristics require sustained global search without sacrificing local refinement, yet many variable-structure methods change operators through one-way iteration schedules. We introduce the Weather State Ants Optimizer (WSAO), in which a discrete-time Markov chain recurrently selects one of three population updates. Sunny, cloudy, and rainy states correspond to global exploration, movement toward nests, and local refinement, respectively. An archive-based mechanism also maintains several spatially separated nests as concurrent search centers. Thirty independent runs compared WSAO with 11 algorithms on 29 CEC2017 and 12 CEC2022 functions. WSAO achieved the lowest Friedman mean rank on both suites, at 2.48 and 2.33. Across five constrained design cases, it joined the leading group by mean objective value on four cases and ranked second on pressure-vessel design. Targeted CEC2022 controls showed that no alternative transition matrix dominated the baseline. Eliminating the trial perturbation worsened every selected function, whereas the contribution of multiple nests depended on the landscape structure. The combined evidence supports recurrent state-controlled search as a competitive framework for continuous numerical and constrained optimization.

title: Kepemilikan Hak Cipta atas Karya yang Dihasilkan oleh Artificial Intelligence (AI): Studi Perbandingan Hukum Indonesia, Amerika Serikat dan Inggris
abstract: Perkembangan teknologi kecerdasan buatan (Artificial Intelligence/AI) telah menimbulkan tantangan baru dalam sistem hukum hak kekayaan intelektual, khususnya dalam penentuan kepemilikan hak cipta. AI kini mampu menghasilkan karya kreatif yang memiliki nilai orisinalitas tinggi, seperti teks, musik, dan gambar, tanpa keterlibatan signifikan dari manusia. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaturan hukum terkait hak cipta atas karya yang dihasilkan oleh AI dalam perspektif hukum Indonesia, Amerika Serikat, dan Inggris. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah penelitian hukum normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan, konseptual, dan komparatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem hukum Indonesia masih berpegang pada prinsip human authorship requirement, di mana hanya manusia yang dapat diakui sebagai pencipta. Sebaliknya, Inggris melalui Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 telah memberikan pengakuan terbatas terhadap karya yang dihasilkan komputer, dengan menyebut bahwa pencipta adalah pihak yang mengatur proses penciptaan karya tersebut. Amerika Serikat tetap mempertahankan prinsip bahwa hak cipta hanya berlaku pada karya manusia yang tertulis dalam U.S. Copyright Act. Berdasarkan temuan ini, disimpulkan bahwa Indonesia perlu melakukan pembaruan regulasi guna mengakomodasi perkembangan teknologi AI agar tercipta kepastian hukum bagi para pencipta dan pelaku industri kreatif.

title: Consultant-Led Innovation Strategies: Driving Business Growth Through Machine Learning in Tech, Education, and Retail
abstract: Abstract This chapter examines how consultants enable businesses to adopt machine learning. The Philippines will provide examples, with an emphasis on three sectors where consultants have been actively employed: retail, education, and technology. In these settings, consultants do much more than just introduce new technology. Instead, it is one where consultants use organizational culture-appropriate practices to translate technological potential. They facilitate organizations to navigate through skill gaps, fragmented data, and resistance to change. This chapter will identify how consultants help organizations in technology transition toward predictive and user-centric systems, education toward adaptive and data-informed learning environments, and in retail toward applying machine learning for pricing, inventory management, and customer engagement. Throughout all these examples, it is not technological skills but the consultant’s capacity to read between contexts that play a critical role. This chapter will conclude by saying that innovation by consultants can pave the way for faster digital transformation in emerging economies if these are made participative, contextual, and oriented toward long-term organizational capacity building.

title: Approximate cubic phase states in a trapped ion
abstract: Universal quantum computation with continuous variables cannot be attained solely with a set of Gaussian operations, it requires the addition of a non-Gaussian element, at least of third order in the quadrature operators, such as the cubic phase state. In this work, we present a method to generate a quantum state in the vibrational mode of a trapped ion that exhibits characteristics compatible with the cubic phase state, such as the distinctive oscillating pattern in its Wigner function. This state emerges from the nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings interaction native to the trapped-ion model, and under the assumption of an initial coherent vibrational state with a large occupation number. Consequently, the evolved vibrational state approximates the cubic phase state with high fidelity, and we use the variance of a nonlinear combination of the quadratures to characterize it. Finally, we provide an analytical expression for its cubicity that shows the high performance of the approximate vibrational cubic phase state.

title: A quantum oracle separation between QMA(2) and QMA
abstract: We find a quantum oracle relative to which $\mathsf{QMA} \neq \mathsf{QMA}(2)$. As a consequence, we resolve the no-disentanglers conjecture of Watrous: for every $ε+δ<1$, any $(ε,δ)$-disentangler requires input size exponential in the number of output qubits. Our proof combines the unitarily invariant polynomial method of She and Yuen (ITCS '23) with a new construction based on the symmetric and antisymmetric subspace projectors, reducing the $\mathsf{QMA}$ lower bound to the approximate degree of $\mathrm{OR}$.

title: Linear Fusion MultiDiffusion for Fast Training-Free Spherical Panorama Generation
abstract: We propose LF-MultiDiffusion, a training-free panorama generation method that extends MultiDiffusion to support linear projections between target and reference image spaces. Our key idea is to reformulate latent aggregation as a regularized least-squares problem and solve it efficiently with a Krylov-based iterative solver inside the denoising loop. This formulation enables denser and more natural mappings than prior training-free methods, yielding more stable generation with far fewer perspective views. As a result, LF-MultiDiffusion reduces the number of image generator evaluations during denoising and significantly improves inference efficiency. Experiments show that LF-MultiDiffusion achieves better visual quality, text alignment, and panoramic consistency than the strongest training-free baseline, while providing a 15.36$\times$ speedup. Our project page is available at: https://ahykw.github.io/lfmd.

title: MASkills: Continual Skills Optimization for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems have shown strong performance on complex tasks, yet continual improvement from interaction experience remains challenging. Existing self-reflection methods build experience memories, but memories are mostly hard to invoke, refine, or scale, while agent skills offer a more actionable unit: structured procedural knowledge that specifies when to act, how to act, and which resources or tools to use. We introduce MASkills, a continual learning framework that optimizes multi-agent LLM systems through agent skills. MASkills presents a new agent-optimization pipeline that integrates skill-conditioned credit assignment, hierarchical credit aggregation, and momentum-smoothed optimization, enabling agent skill libraries to evolve through refinement, induction, consolidation, and pruning. Experiments on HotpotQA, LoCoMo, and GAIA demonstrate the effectiveness of MASkills across multiple agentic tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/DaRL-GenAI/MASkills

title: Auditory Illusion Benchmark for Large Audio Language Models
abstract: Perceptual illusions have long served as crucial probes into human cognition, revealing biases and limitations of perception. In the auditory domain, such illusions provide a unique lens for testing whether Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) replicate human perceptual tendencies. Despite their importance, most benchmarks focus on visual illusions or general audio tasks, leaving auditory illusions underexplored. To this end, we present AIB, the first auditory illusion benchmark for LALMs, covering ten representative illusions across music, sound, and speech, each annotated for the presence of knowledge-based priors. Our methodology pairs model evaluation with controlled human listening studies, enabling direct comparison of responses. Results show systematic differences: while most LALMs remain signal-faithful on low-level acoustic illusions, several exhibit more human-like responses when linguistic or musical priors are involved, although no model matches the human perceptual profile. These findings highlight the current limitations of LALMs as cognitive models. By establishing auditory illusions as a rigorous testbed, our work offers a new perspective for probing neural black-box models and advancing understanding of auditory cognition. AIB is publicly available at https://github.com/gillosae/aib.

title: A Comparative Study of Graph Representations for GNN-Based Power Grid Control in L2RPN
abstract: Graph construction is a critical but underexamined design choice in deep reinforcement learning for power grid control. We present a controlled experimental comparison of different graph representations, including physical topology, electrical-sensitivity, and hybrid variants for topology control in the Learning to Run a Power Network (L2RPN) environment. Our findings indicate that matching graph complexity to task granularity is more important than maximizing representational richness, and highlight the importance of controlled representation studies at scale.

title: SelfLift: Accelerating Few-Step Diffusion via Self-Recovering Resolution Transition
abstract: Few-step diffusion models substantially compress temporal computation, making the spatial cost of each model evaluation an increasingly dominant source of inference latency. Progressive-resolution inference reduces this cost by performing early denoising at low resolution and reserving high-resolution computation for refinement. However, existing methods typically lift intermediate latents directly and rely on subsequent steps to absorb the induced distribution mismatch. In the few-step regime, the limited recovery budget leaves these errors as visible artifacts, constraining how late the transition can occur and, consequently, how efficiently it can be performed. We introduce SelfLift, a self-recovering progressive-resolution framework that derives both transition-repair signals and trajectory-aligned supervision from the generative model itself. SelfLift-zero proposes a training-free Artifact-Aware Consistency Lift, using disagreement between direct latent lifting and pixel-VAE re-encoding as both a localized artifact-risk signal and a model-native correction direction. It enables reliable late transitions without external super-resolution, extra denoiser evaluations, or sampling-schedule modifications. Building on this robust transition, SelfLift-rich performs On-Policy Self Recovery on student-visited states, transferring dense high-resolution guidance from an internal self-teacher while remaining aligned with the altered progressive-resolution dynamics. Across FLUX.2-Klein and Z-Image-Turbo, SelfLift reduces end-to-end latency by 41.5% and 44.1%, respectively. Combined with timestep distillation, it delivers overall speedups of 29.61x and 19.21x over the corresponding 50-step models while preserving competitive generation quality, establishing a stronger speed-quality frontier for few-step diffusion.

title: Team DArgk at the 2026 ELOQUENT lab for evaluating generative language model quality: Residuals of Humanity: AI Detection Evasion via GRPO Fine-Tuning
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent and coherent text that is increasingly difficult to distinguish from human writing, motivating the development of automatic AI-generated text detectors. However, the robustness of such detectors under adversarial generation remains uncertain. This paper presents SHADE (Stochastic Human-like generation via Adversarial Detector Evasion), a reinforcement learning framework that formulates detector evasion as a policy optimization problem. Instead of applying post-hoc perturbations or prompting-based rewriting, SHADE fine-tunes an instruction-tuned LLaMA model with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), using feedback from a surrogate detector based on the PAN 2025 mdok system. Our experiments show that full fine-tuning with a small KL regularization penalty achieves $98.5\%$ surrogate evasion, compared to $1.5\%$ for the base model, while LoRA-based adaptation is substantially less effective under regularization. Linguistic analysis reveals that successful evasion is associated with shorter, simpler, and less lexically diverse outputs, suggesting that high detector evasion does not necessarily correspond to more human-like writing. In the official Voight-Kampff competition setting, our submissions ranked sixth and seventh, indicating that optimization against a single surrogate detector only partially transfers to unseen evaluation classifiers. These results highlight both the potential and limitations of reinforcement learning for adversarial AI-text generation and motivate more robust, multi-detector evaluation protocols for AI-generated text detection.

title: Extending the computational reach of quantum annealing using reverse annealing
abstract: Abstract Quantum annealing is a promising heuristic for combinatorial optimization, but on current hardware its solution quality degrades for larger and more complex problems due to noise and small energy gaps. Reverse annealing has been established as a refinement strategy, yet it remains unclear how problem characteristics, particularly the implemented quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) matrix structure, influence refinement success and the optimal parameter regime. We find that combining forward and reverse annealing improves solution quality, with the magnitude of the improvement depending strongly on the problem class and corresponding QUBO size, while efficiency gains are tied to both annealing and problem-instance parameters. The benefits of reverse annealing increase with problem complexity and are strongest in regimes where forward annealing is increasingly limited. In these settings, reverse annealing yields larger efficiency gains than simply extending forward annealing times. We establish these results through a systematic experimental study on a D-Wave Advantage system, benchmarking reverse annealing across Max-Cut, Number Partitioning, and sparse clustering problems while varying reverse distance, pause duration, and annealing time. We identify optimal reverse annealing parameter regimes that depend on QUBO characteristics and are consistent with expected freeze-out behavior and with the energy-level-crossing structure observed for small representative instances. These findings demonstrate that reverse annealing is most valuable for large, high-complexity optimization problems and is likely to gain importance as quantum annealing hardware scales toward more realistic applications.

evidence.title: Extending the computational reach of Quantum Annealing using Reverse Annealing
evidence.abstract: Quantum annealing is a promising heuristic for combinatorial optimization, but on current hardware its performance degrades for larger and more complex problems due to noise and small energy gaps. Reverse annealing has been proposed as a refinement strategy, yet it remains unclear when it provides systematic advantages over standard forward annealing or simply increasing annealing time. We find that combining forward and reverse annealing consistently improves solution quality and efficiency across multiple problem classes. The benefits of reverse annealing increase with problem complexity and are strongest in regimes where forward annealing is increasingly limited. Moreover, reverse annealing yields larger efficiency gains than simply extending forward annealing times. We establish these results through a systematic experimental study on a D-Wave Advantage system, benchmarking reverse annealing across Max-Cut, Number Partitioning, and sparse clustering problems while varying reverse distance, pause duration, and annealing time. We identify a narrow optimal regime for reverse annealing parameters linked to the location of freeze-out points and energy-level crossings in the annealing schedule. These findings demonstrate that reverse annealing is most valuable for large, high-complexity optimization problems and is likely to gain importance as quantum annealing hardware scales toward more realistic applications.

title: A Resource-Aware Hybrid Quantum-Classical Framework for Network Intrusion Detection with Selective Quantum Processing
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) is increasingly investigated for network intrusion detection, but the practical value of current quantum models remains uncertain because many studies rely on small simulated data sets, idealized execution, weak classical baselines, or isolated accuracy comparisons. This study develops and evaluates a resource-aware hybrid quantum-classical intrusion detection framework that combines fixed fidelity quantum kernels, repaired Quantum Kernel Alignment (QKA), a Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC), LightGBM, prototype-based kernel reduction, and probabilistic stacking. Experiments use the UNSW-NB15 benchmark under a leakage-aware preprocessing protocol and repeated evaluation across five random seeds. The experimental program covers 4- and 6-qubit representations, multiple training sizes, prototype budgets, and finite-shot configurations, yielding 260 experimental configurations/runs. The strongest quantum-assisted model, a 6-qubit QKA-VQC-LightGBM stack at 100 samples per class, obtains mean F1=0.8480, MCC=0.7092, ROC-AUC=0.9398, and PR-AUC=0.9302. Repaired QKA improves F1 from 0.8043 for the corresponding fixed kernel to 0.8089, while 50-prototype QKA attains F1=0.8257 with a more favorable kernel-workload trade-off than larger prototype budgets. Finite-shot experiments between 1,024 and 4,096 shots remain stable in simulation. However, full-data LightGBM remains stronger overall (F1=0.8957, MCC=0.8068, ROC-AUC=0.9755, PR-AUC=0.9704), and corrected statistical tests do not establish general quantum superiority. These findings motivate a Selective Quantum Intrusion Detection System (S-QIDS), in which classical inference handles high-confidence traffic and quantum processing is reserved for uncertain, novel, or high-risk observations. The study therefore reframes near-term quantum intrusion detection from unconditional quantum advantage toward measurable quantum utility, quantum-classical complementarity, and resource-aware quantum intervention.

title: Protocol for Cognitive Synergy in Human–AI Cooperation
abstract: This paper presents the Protocol for Cognitive Synergy in Human–AI Cooperation as a methodological framework for structuring the joint cognitive process of humans and artificial intelligence in knowledge creation. The Protocol is based on the functional complementarity of two different cognitive systems. It operationalizes their cooperation through a recursive process that includes human epistemic problem framing, AI analytical expansion, iterative human–AI co-structuring of reasoning, joint epistemic validation, consensus assessment, joint knowledge output development, and outcome evaluation. Decision gates between specific phases allow advancement only when relevant quality criteria are met. Failure to meet these criteria activates a return to a previous or other relevant phase. Special attention is given to potential errors of the human, the AI, and the structure of their interaction. These include source issues, AI hallucinations, semantic drift, cognitive biases, propagation of erroneous premises, and false consensus. Human and AI contributions are functionally different. However, claims within the joint process are epistemically evaluated based on the quality of reasoning, evidential grounding, coherence, and contribution to the joint output. Disagreement can serve to expand the solution space and stabilize argumentation. If sufficient convergence is not achieved after appropriate verification, the final decision and responsibility remain human. The operational diagram and the methodological table for problem identification, corrective action, resolution criteria, and return or continuation conditions represent the central instrument of the Protocol. The purpose of the Protocol is to increase the reliability of joint knowledge creation through a stable, disciplined, transparent, verifiable, and recursive interaction.

title: HBPC: Reproducibility Package for Exact Hierarchical Boundary Optimization for Hard-Limited Multilingual Document Chunking
abstract: Reproducibility compendium for HBPC, an exact lexicographic dynamic-programming method for hard-limited multilingual document chunking. The deposit preserves the internally frozen protocol, implementation, exact FLORESv1 input archive, and all 3,840 archived raw records unchanged. Separately labeled post-hoc materials provide corrected source-offset metrics, pair-stratified bootstrap intervals, an independent-boundary audit, an equal-input shared-signal greedy comparison, generated figures and tables, and the corresponding manuscript. The freeze is self-attested and is not represented as an externally timestamped preregistration. This is a mixed-license deposit: author-owned code is GPL-3.0-only; the manuscript and author-created research materials are CC-BY-4.0; the bundled FLORESv1 archive remains CC-BY-SA-4.0. See LICENSES.md for exact scope and attribution.

title: Autocatalytic Closure: An AGI Research Program Based on Non-equilibrium Thermodynamics
abstract: Autocatalytic Closure: An AGI Research Program Based on Non-equilibrium Thermodynamics Wang Fengqing(School of Automation Engineering, Northeast Electric Power University, Jilin 132012, China) Abstract: [Objective] This paper addresses four puzzles in artificial intelligence, the diminishing returns of scaling, persistent hallucination, catastrophic forgetting, and inexhaustible tail risk, which have so far been discussed separately without a unified explanation. [Methods] Adopting non-equilibrium thermodynamics as a programmatic language, it proposes the establishment of an autocatalytic closure as the physical criterion for AGI, together with a trinity of high-entropy exploration, low-entropy selection and organogenesis, operationalized by a three-gate mechanism; a two-stage correction experiment (N=2) serves as a proof-of-concept. [Results] The four puzzles are uniformly attributed to the heterocatalytic open-loop nature of current systems; drawing on the Anthropic 2026 report and self-verification precedents, the paper diagnoses that frontier practice still operates in the open-loop stage. [Limitations] The N=2 experiment is only a mechanistic illustration, and the engineering feasibility of the three-gate mechanism remains unverified. [Conclusions] The criterion of AGI should be the establishment of an autocatalytic closure, and falsifiable schemes are provided. Keywords: autocatalytic closure; dissipative structure; low-entropy selection; organogenesis emergence; AGI criterion

title: Quantum Topology and Machine Learning Synergy: A Collaborative Optimization Framework
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of physics, offers unique properties that could revolutionize machine learning. This paper investigates the potential of combining quantum topology with machine learning to achieve enhanced data analysis and predictive modeling. We propose a novel framework that leverages the inherent characteristics of quantum topology to create a synergistic approach, enabling more robust and accurate results. The core mechanism involves incorporating quantum algorithms into machine learning models, which, in turn, facilitates a deeper understanding of complex datasets. The resulting framework offers a new optimization approach, pushing the boundaries of current machine learning techniques. This work demonstrates the potential of quantum topology to significantly enhance data analysis and model prediction, presenting a fundamentally new pathway for optimizing complex systems.
