title: Estrategias de marketing impulsadas por inteligencia artificial: su rol en la toma de decisiones organizacionales
abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) reordena el marketing contemporáneo y se ha consolidado como un factor estratégico para la competitividad de las organizaciones. Este estudio analiza cómo la literatura académica reciente caracteriza la incorporación de la IA en las estrategias de marketing y las implicaciones que se le atribuyen para la toma de decisiones organizacionales y para la personalización de la experiencia del cliente. El enfoque es cualitativo, con diseño documental de carácter narrativo estructurado. Se revisó literatura recuperada de Scopus y Web of Science, circunscrita al período 2014-2024 y analizada mediante matrices de categorías temáticas y codificación con el software ATLAS.ti 23. Tras un cribado documental que identificó 38 fuentes primarias elegibles, el corpus analítico quedó conformado por 11 fuentes seleccionadas por su densidad de contenido empírico y calidad académica. Se identificaron 313 citas codificadas en 12 códigos, agrupados en tres familias: herramientas de IA en marketing (139 citas), barreras de implementación (99 citas) y transformación de la relación marca-consumidor (75 citas). Las herramientas más adoptadas sistemas de recomendación, chatbots, analítica predictiva y automatización publicitaria elevan la eficiencia operativa y las tasas de conversión según los estudios revisados. A partir de los hallazgos se propone un modelo interpretativo que articula las tres familias en una secuencia condicional: la adopción tecnológica se traduce en ventaja competitiva solo cuando supera el filtro de las barreras de implementación y cuando la organización gobierna la tensión entre la personalización, que exige datos, y la confianza, que exige transparencia y control sobre esos datos. Se concluye que ese equilibrio, y no la mera adopción, determina la sostenibilidad de la ventaja. Se sugiere avanzar hacia estudios longitudinales y de alcance regional que validen empíricamente estos hallazgos en contextos latinoamericanos.

title: METHODOLOGY OF LINGUISTICS: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON HYPOTHESIS-MAKING
abstract: The methodology of linguistics has historically been shaped by the interplay between observation, theory construction, data selection, and explanatory adequacy.From philological comparison and structural analysis to generative formalization and corpus-based description, linguistic inquiry has repeatedly redefined how hypotheses are formed, tested, and revised.The rise of artificial intelligence, especially machine learning and large language models, introduces a new methodological moment.Aritficial intelligence systems can process massive multilingual corpora, detect latent patterns, generate candidate generalizations, simulate judgments, and support exploratory analysis at unprecedented scale.At the same time, they raise serious epistemological concerns: opacity, bias, overfitting to surface distributions, conflation of correlation with explanation, and the risk of outsourcing theoretical reasoning to statistical systems.This article examines how aritficial intelligence is reshaping linguistic hypothesis-making.It argues that aritficial intelligence should be understood neither as a replacement for linguistic theory nor as a neutral computational aid, but as a transformative methodological instrument that changes the pace, scale, and form of hypothesis generation.The article situates hypothesis-making within major traditions of linguistic methodology.It then defines basic methodological functions of aritficial intelligence in linguistic hypothesis-making and analyzes its specific contributions to hypothesis generation across subfields of morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, historical linguistics, and sociolinguistics.The discussion highlights how aritficial intelligence can expand the empirical horizon of linguistics by revealing nonobvious regularities and enabling more dynamic interactions between data and theory.It also shows that AI-generated hypotheses remain dependent on data quality, annotation regimes, modeling choices, and human interpretation.The conclusion is that the future of linguistic methodology lies in a reflexive partnership between computational systems and theoretically informed researchers.In that partnership, aritficial intelligence can accelerate discovery, though explanatory accountability should remain a human scholarly responsibility.

title: TRACE: A spatiotemporal contact memory graph network simulator for granular dynamics
abstract: Learned graph simulators provide an efficient alternative to high-fidelity solvers for granular dynamics. However, granular motion depends strongly on inter-granular contact history, which is difficult to preserve when particle contacts form, break, and rearrange. Existing simulators mainly store temporal information in node features or node-level memory. Here we introduce TRACE, a graph-network simulator that stores interaction history directly on contact edges. Each edge maintains a persistent memory updated by attention-based message passing and a gated recurrent unit, while an edge-identity dictionary preserves this memory as the contact graph changes. A physics-structured decoder predicts inter-granular normal and tangential contact forces, enforces the Coulomb friction limit, and applies equal-and-opposite internal forces. The model is trained with single-step pretraining followed by autoregressive rollout fine-tuning. We evaluate TRACE on 2D and 3D granular column-collapse benchmarks. In both cases, TRACE produces stable, physically consistent long-horizon rollouts, closely reproducing the final deposit geometry and the kinetic energy released during collapse. evidence.title: TRACE: A spatiotemporal contact memory graph network simulator for granular dynamics
evidence.abstract: Learned graph simulators provide an efficient alternative to high-fidelity solvers for granular dynamics. However, granular motion depends strongly on inter-granular contact history, which is difficult to preserve when particle contacts form, break, and rearrange. Existing simulators mainly store temporal information in node features or node-level memory. Here we introduce TRACE, a graph-network simulator that stores interaction history directly on contact edges. Each edge maintains a persistent memory updated by attention-based message passing and a gated recurrent unit, while an edge-identity dictionary preserves this memory as the contact graph changes. A physics-structured decoder predicts inter-granular normal and tangential contact forces, enforces the Coulomb friction limit, and applies equal-and-opposite internal forces. The model is trained with single-step pretraining followed by autoregressive rollout fine-tuning. We evaluate TRACE on 2D and 3D granular column-collapse benchmarks. In both cases, TRACE produces stable, physically consistent long-horizon rollouts, closely reproducing the final deposit geometry and the kinetic energy released during collapse. Compared with graph network simulator (GNS) and node-memory graph neural simulator (NMGNS), TRACE reduces long-rollout position error by 31-62% and final-deposit error by 58-89% across the two benchmarks, while using fewer parameters and maintaining near-zero particle interpenetration. TRACE also achieves 12.2$\times$ and 8.9$\times$ speedups over the material point method (MPM) reference solver in 2D and 3D, respectively. title: LexIssue: Benchmarking Legal Issue Identification in Chinese Civil Litigation
abstract: Identifying the issues disputed between litigating parties is a crucial component of real-world litigation. However, legal issues remain comparatively underexplored in legal AI research. In this work, we study the computational modelling of legal issue identification in litigation. We introduce a legally grounded hierarchical schema that represents legal issues through both free-form issue descriptions and structured legal categories, and formulate legal issue identification as two complementary tasks: legal issue generation and legal issue classification. Based on this formulation, we construct LexIssue, a benchmark containing 430 real-world Chinese civil litigation cases and 1,303 expert-annotated disputed legal issues. We further develop an issue-centric legal knowledge base spanning 27 causes of action and 441 candidate legal issue entries to support retrieval-augmented reasoning. Experimental results across a diverse set of models show that retrieval-augmented generation using the constructed legal issue knowledge base consistently improves performance in identifying disputed legal issues and their corresponding legal attributes.

title: Beyond Problem Solving: Large Language Models for Emotional and Reflective Support in Mathematics Learning
abstract: Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITSs) traditionally focus their adaptive support on cognitive aspects of learning. Although effective, little is known about how such systems can be enhanced by addressing students' emotional states. In particular, the role of mindful interventions for supporting student learning and experiences in adaptive math learning remains underexplored. We developed "Math with Matt", an ITS that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to provide both cognitive and emotional support in algebra learning. The system offers 1) an LLM-based mindful chat that delivers context-sensitive emotional support through a pedagogical agent Matt, and 2) mindful feedback and hint messages (not just evaluative) to enhance learning experiences and reduce math anxiety. We conducted a classroom study with 7th graders, comparing a Mindful version against a version with cognitive support only. Overall, the ITS reduced executive state-math anxiety and improved students' math learning, though no significant differences emerged between the conditions. However, students with the mindfulness interventions showed higher learning efficiency and well-balanced problem-solving behavior, since they achieve a similar level of math learning with less learning time and fewer requested hints compared to the Cognitive version. Additionally, they reported that the pedagogical agent felt more supportive and caring than students in the cognitive condition. Our study demonstrates the feasibility and scalability of integrating mindfulness into ITSs through LLM-based interactions and positions LLMs as an adaptive, socio-emotional layer within cognitive math tutoring.

title: LeakageBench: Document-Level Leakage Risk for Redacting Personally Identifiable Information in Document Images
abstract: Real-world personally identifiable information (PII) redaction often operates on document images---scans, screenshots, and PDF renderings---where OCR errors, layout structure, and visual noise determine whether sensitive information is actually removed. Existing PII benchmarks are mostly text-centric and do not measure document-level redaction risk: a page remains unsafe if even one identifier is missed. We introduce LeakageBench, a challenge set of 500 document images with 11,954 GDPR-aligned PII annotations spanning direct identifiers, linkage keys, and contextual re-identification surfaces. We evaluate generic OCR pipelines, commercial and task-adapted OCR-dependent detectors, and OCR-free vision-language models using entity-level F1, group-wise leakage, and document-level leakage metrics. Code Interpreter raises GPT-5.5 localization F1 from 0.090 to 0.249, but critical page-level leakage remains 0.968. These results show that stronger detection and tool assistance improve localization without making most pages safe for release. LeakageBench provides a diagnostic benchmark for high-recall, spatially grounded PII redaction in document images.

title: Task-Level Natural Language Priors as Learning Signals for Low-Resource LLM Training
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often struggle when low-resource training data are ambiguous or incomplete. Task-level natural-language priors can provide useful guidance in such settings, but existing approaches usually treat these priors as input context rather than as learning signals during training. We study how task-level natural-language priors can supply guidance missing from these data through Prior-Guided Tuning (PGT). Its implementation, Contrastive Prior Steering (CPS), retains the supervised objective and adds positive- and negative-prior-conditioned losses with opposing optimization directions. Across AmbiMath, Diagnostic Anchoring, and Jigsaw, CPS achieves near-perfect exact-match accuracy on the synthetic task, improves accuracy under misleading diagnostic suggestions by 8.2 percentage points, and improves average subgroup Macro F1 on Jigsaw by 10.7 percentage points over plain fine-tuning, averaged over the two evaluated models. On Jigsaw, with one tenth of the experimental training data, CPS slightly exceeds full-data plain fine-tuning. These results show how reusable task-level language can complement limited labeled examples without requiring instance-level rationales or preference pairs.

title: TRATADO DA CRITICIDADE METAESTÁVEL, DO COLAPSO INTERVALAR E DA ENGENHARIA PERMUTADORA MATRICIAL DE ANACRÓSTICOS AXIOMÁTICOS HIPERCONTEXTUAIS de KNOPP-Fellipe
abstract: Este tratado formaliza o modelo da Permutadora Matricial de Knopp-Fellipe como ferramenta de engenharia textual e modelagem fenomenológica. Analisa-se o colapso do espaço latente quando o intervalo de mediação o transubjetiva converge assintoticamente a zero, gerando o fenômeno do colapso de dados sintéticos em sistemas autorregressivos. Propõe-se uma formulações matemática estocástica e critérios de validação laboratorial para salvaguardar a dinamicidade dos sistemas cognitivos artificiais e biológicos.

title: ACADEMIC LITERATURE REVIEW AND STATISTICAL EVIDENCE BASE
abstract: Machine translation (MT) involving Uzbek and Karakalpak occupies a distinctive position in contemporary computational linguistics: both languages are Turkic, agglutinative, and classified as low-resource within the meaning established by Koehn and Knowles (2017) , who identify data scarcity, domain mismatch, and rare-word handling as the principal obstacles to high-quality neural machine translation (NMT). This review synthesises verifiable, source-traceable evidence across four analytical levels — international/foreign, CIS-regional, Uzbekistan, and Karakalpakstan research — culminating in a consolidated reference list. Statistical figures cited below (BLEU, chrF, word error rate, corpus size in sentence pairs) are reproduced directly from the cited primary sources and are not estimated or invented.

title: Memory-Adaptive Machine Learning (MAML)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm, MAML, based on the concept of dynamic memory adaptation. Traditional machine learning methods often struggle with adapting to changing data distributions, limiting their generalization capabilities. MAML addresses this challenge by dynamically adjusting the model's memory capacity and storage structure, allowing the model to learn more effectively from new data. We present a theoretical framework and a practical implementation of MAML, demonstrating its ability to significantly improve model performance on a range of benchmark datasets. The core mechanism involves a learning rate-based adjustment of the model's parameters, iteratively refining the model to better represent the input data. This adaptive approach fosters improved generalization and robustness.

title: Quantum Information in Error Correcting Computation Framework
abstract: Quantum information processing offers a paradigm shift in computation, particularly in areas demanding high accuracy and resilience against errors. This paper presents a novel quantum information processing framework, termed "Quantum Error Correction with Entangled State Manipulation," designed to address the challenges of non-linear computations. We propose a mechanism leveraging quantum entanglement to automatically correct errors during the execution of complex calculations. This approach significantly improves computational precision and stability compared to traditional error correction methods. The core of this framework involves the creation and manipulation of entangled quantum states to facilitate error correction, offering a promising path towards more robust and accurate quantum computations. The paper explores the potential of this framework to tackle challenging problems in quantum algorithms, emphasizing the benefits of leveraging quantum entanglement for error mitigation.

title: Dimension Smoothness and Quantum Entanglement Coupling Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dimension smoothness techniques combined with quantum entanglement to achieve precise control and measurement of quantum states. We introduce a novel coupling algorithm based on quantum entanglement, which leverages the inherent properties of entanglement to optimize the smoothing process of quantum states. This approach aims to improve the accuracy and stability of quantum systems compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism involves incorporating entanglement's 'coherence' to enhance the smoothing of the quantum state, ultimately providing a more precise and stable system. The theoretical foundations are built upon the principles of quantum mechanics and the intricacies of dimension smoothness. The paper highlights the potential of this new coupling approach to address limitations in quantum control and prediction.

title: Hypergraph Neural Networks for Representing Hierarchical Relationships
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and drug discovery. However, many real-world datasets exhibit complex hierarchical relationships that GNNs struggle to capture effectively. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing Hypergraph Neural Networks (HGNNs) to represent and reason about these hierarchies. HGNNs extend the concept of GNNs by operating on hypergraphs, where nodes can have multiple connections, explicitly modeling relationships like parent-child, supervisor-subordinate, or broader structural connections. We demonstrate that this approach significantly improves the representation and reasoning capabilities of neural networks when dealing with hierarchical data. The core contribution lies in adapting the GNN framework to hypergraph structures, allowing for the direct encoding of hierarchical information and leading to more accurate predictions and insights. This work provides a foundation for future research in applying HGNNs to diverse hierarchical datasets and exploring more sophisticated hypergraph architectures.

title: Algorithmic Evolutionary Sampling for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper introduces Algorithmic Evolutionary Sampling (AES), a novel approach to exploring the solution space of complex systems utilizing evolutionary sampling. Complex systems often exhibit intricate and non-linear relationships, making traditional optimization methods insufficient. AES leverages the strengths of evolutionary algorithms – particularly genetic algorithms – combined with Bayesian optimization to intelligently navigate this space. The core mechanism involves iteratively refining a search strategy through a probabilistic assessment of potential solutions, prioritizing novel regions and mitigating local optima. The resulting algorithm demonstrates improved performance compared to existing methods in a series of simulated complex system scenarios. This research focuses on providing a robust and adaptable framework for tackling challenges inherent in modeling and analyzing dynamic systems.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A Comparative Analysis Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 自适应拓扑的量子态共振
abstract: Quantum state resonance is a fundamental process in quantum systems, crucial for various applications, including quantum computation and quantum information processing. Conventional approaches often rely on static resonance conditions, limiting the system's adaptability. This paper explores the potential of utilizing adaptive topology to design a novel quantum state resonance control technique. We investigate a mechanism that leverages the inherent dynamic properties of adaptive topology to dynamically adjust the resonance parameters, enhancing stability and potentially enabling new functionalities. The core claim focuses on the development of a technique that dynamically adjusts resonance parameters based on the system's state, fostering a more robust and versatile quantum state resonance. This research addresses limitations of traditional methods and proposes a new pathway towards more adaptable and controllable quantum phenomena.

title: E8-Phased Selmer Resonance for Quantum Secure Communication — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By mapping the 240 E8 root vectors onto a 132 Hz phase lattice modulated by the golden ratio, we generate a quasi‑periodic interference field whose spectral fingerprints encode the distribution of 2‑Selmer groups over function fields. The resulting E8‑phased signal can be sampled by quantum sensors to recover a shared secret that is statistically tied to the Selmer group structure, providing a new quantum key‑distribution protocol that is provably resistant to attacks exploiting Selmer‑group heuristics. This principle extends the Poonen–Rains power‑law corrections by embedding them in a physical phase coherence framework, and leverages the EuroMillions mining methodology to identify high‑entropy seed vectors from the 240‑root lattice. The approach unifies arithmetic geometry, harmonic analysis, and quantum information into a single E8‑based cryptographic primitive. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Quantum Entanglement Enhanced Distributed Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed quantum computing that leverages the enhancement of quantum entanglement to significantly improve computational efficiency and resilience to errors. Traditional distributed quantum computing suffers from limitations imposed by environmental noise and entanglement degradation. Our method addresses these challenges by actively amplifying entanglement through precise control and manipulation of entangled states. This is achieved utilizing non-classical optical elements and feedback control systems, specifically employing phase control techniques to mitigate the effects of noise and extend the coherence time of entangled states. The core claim of this work is that precise control and enhancement of quantum entanglement can dramatically increase the efficiency and fault tolerance of distributed quantum computation. We outline the theoretical framework, detailing the key mechanisms involved, and discuss the potential impact of this technology.

title: Neuro-Topology Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design and optimization, termed Neuro-Topology Adaptive Learning. The core idea centers on dynamically adjusting the topology of a neural network – its connections and potentially its structural organization – to improve information flow and computational efficiency. Traditional deep learning models often struggle with complex, non-Euclidean data due to limitations in their fixed architectures. This research leverages reinforcement learning to create a "topology controller" that learns to modify the network's connection matrix in real-time, guided by activation patterns, error propagation, and topological constraints. The system aims to minimize global error or maximize the transmission efficiency of specific information features. The key innovation lies in treating the network topology itself as the primary learning object, offering a new level of control and potentially superior performance, particularly for data with inherent topological structures like spatial and temporal data. The algorithm incorporates constraints to maintain local connection strengths and form specific neural clusters, contributing to a more robust and efficient learning process.

evidence.title: Neuro-Topology Adaptive Learning
evidence.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design and optimization, termed Neuro-Topology Adaptive Learning. The core idea centers on dynamically adjusting the topology of a neural network – its connections and potentially its structural organization – to improve information flow and computational efficiency. Traditional deep learning models often struggle with complex, non-Euclidean data due to limitations in their fixed architectures. This research leverages reinforcement learning to create a "topology controller" that learns to modify the network's connection matrix in real-time, guided by activation patterns, error propagation, and topological constraints. The system aims to minimize global error or maximize the transmission efficiency of specific information features. The key innovation lies in treating the network topology itself as the primary learning object, offering a new level of control and potentially superior performance, particularly for data with inherent topological structures like spatial and temporal data. The algorithm incorporates constraints to maintain local connection strengths and form specific neural clusters, contributing to a more robust and efficient learning process.

title: On Dynamic Programming-Based Reinforcement Learning Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic programming principles to optimize reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms. Traditional RL methods often suffer from slow convergence and suboptimal performance due to their reliance on random exploration strategies. We propose a novel framework that leverages the deterministic optimization capabilities of dynamic programming to address these limitations. Specifically, we formulate RL problems as dynamic programming problems, employing techniques to efficiently transition between states and actions. This approach allows us to derive analytically optimal policies, significantly accelerating the learning process and improving the overall performance of RL agents. The core of our methodology lies in transforming the exploration aspect of RL into a structured, systematic optimization process, yielding substantial gains compared to purely stochastic methods. This work contributes to a more efficient and effective paradigm for tackling complex RL challenges. ---

title: 基于量子拓扑的动态量子系统模拟
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum system simulation framework based on quantum topology. Traditional quantum system simulation often relies on static models, limiting the ability to capture the intricate dynamics of quantum systems. Our approach leverages the unique properties of quantum topology to provide a more dynamic and insightful simulation method. The framework utilizes a dynamic topology to model the evolution of quantum systems, enabling the discovery of stable and evolving regimes. This work presents a new method for simulating quantum systems, offering significant advantages in understanding and predicting their behavior.

title: 基于自适应的神经网络结构优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network structure optimization based on adaptive neural network architectures. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, failing to effectively leverage data distribution variations. Our method dynamically adjusts the network's structure through a learned data-driven process, resulting in improved model performance and efficiency. The core mechanism involves learning a dynamic structure that adapts to the data, enabling the network to handle complex and evolving datasets more effectively. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments on various benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and training time compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The results highlight the potential of this adaptive structure optimization technique for a broad range of neural network applications.

title: Synthesising Causal Knowledge with Semantic Technologies
abstract: Motivation: AI systems relying solely on correlations often fail when training and production distributions differ, limiting their utility for reliable decision-making. While incorporating causal knowledge offers a more robust alternative, synthesizing such knowledge from heterogeneous sources remains a fragmented and cognitively demanding task. There is currently a lack of support for integrating, comparing, and resolving discrepancies between multiple, often conflicting, causal graphs. Objectives: We present SoCK (Synthesis of Causal Knowledge), a semantic framework designed to integrate, analyse, and explore causal graphs derived from heterogeneous sources. Our goal is to provide a unified representation of causal knowledge that supports expert-in-the-loop exploration and transforms differing causal graphs into a queryable knowledge base. The framework aims to provide an accessible interface for multiple stakeholders, focusing on knowledge engineers, causal discovery researchers, and domain experts. Methods: Following a requirements-driven design, we developed three core contributions: (i) the SoCK ontology provides a unified formalization of causal graphs and their provenance; (ii) the Causal Knowledge Graph integrates multi-source inputs into a unified knowledge base; and (iii) an Exploration Interface operationalizes complex semantic queries through task-based interactions. Results: We evaluate SoCK using the CausalAssembly benchmark dataset. Results demonstrate that the ontology provides high representational coverage, successfully answering 14 out of 15 competency questions. Furthermore, scenario-based evaluations show that the framework effectively supports stakeholder tasks, such as algorithm selection and structural discrepancy analysis, by enabling systematic comparison and exploration of causal graphs through the interface. Conclusion: SoCK addresses a critical challenge in causal discovery by providing the first semantic infrastructure for managing the heterogeneity and ambiguity inherent in multi-source causal discovery. By integrating fragmented causal knowledge and providing an interactive exploration interface to query complex metadata, the framework offers a systematic foundation for comparing causal models and resolving structural causal discrepancies.

title: ExplainBench: A Reproducibility-First Explainability Benchmark for Trustworthy On-Device Agentic AI in Energy Systems
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) evaluation has matured substantially for static classifiers, yet, to the best of our knowledge, no reproducible benchmark has combined explanation-quality evaluation with the on-device, energy-system-specific setting this paper addresses — smart-grid edge controllers, home and building energy management agents, industrial energy IoT, electric-vehicle charging and vehicle-to-grid systems, and renewable microgrid controllers. ExplainBench evaluates explanation quality within agentic decision workflows; it does not evaluate agent capability, autonomy, or intelligence, and provides no runtime assurance or control function. This paper introduces ExplainBench, the fourth module of the BQEB (BIO-Quantum Energy Brain) research program. Consistent with the architecture established across Papers 1–3, ExplainBench introduces no new architectural layer: it registers as the fourth module of the existing Benchmark Layer, alongside ForecastBench, SecBench, and FoundationBench, and records the reproducibility metadata, attribution provenance, and human-rating protocols this evaluation requires within the existing Software and Governance Layer registries, rather than defining parallel mechanisms. The framework specifies nine component metrics — faithfulness, fidelity, stability, consistency, actionability, uncertainty awareness, human interpretability, computational efficiency, and deployment suitability — formally aggregated into six composite indices: the Explainability Quality Index (EQI), Explanation Stability Score (ESS), Counterfactual Consistency Score (CCS), Energy Decision Transparency Score (EDTS), Human Interpretability Rating (HIR), and Explanation Efficiency Index (EEI), assembled into an Explainability Reliability Matrix across a registry of eight forecasting architectures and eight explanation methods. Six algorithms specify benchmark execution, per-instance metric computation, counterfactual scoring, composite aggregation, cross-model statistical comparison, and leaderboard generation, each with explicit complexity bounds. This manuscript defines benchmark infrastructure; it reports no executed evaluations, and every planned-output table in this manuscript is explicitly marked reserved for future experimental validation, consistent with the evidentiary discipline established in Papers 1–3.

title: Physics-guided temporal fusion transformer for probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasting under weather regime shifts
abstract: Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is critical for secure grid operation and economic dispatch, yet its performance is often degraded by non-stationary irradiance fluctuations induced by cloud transients and weather regime shifts. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a physics-guided temporal fusion architecture built on the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) for multi-horizon probabilistic PV forecasting. The model fuses historical plant measurements, Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) variables, and solar-geometry features, and introduces a cross-attention fusion module to align future meteorological drivers with the most relevant historical context for improved ramp responsiveness. Physical plausibility is promoted by soft physics-consistency regularization, including non-negativity, rated-capacity bounds, clear-sky envelope constraints, and ramp-rate penalties, while uncertainty is quantified via multi-quantile regression to produce calibrated prediction intervals. Experiments on real-world PV datasets across different seasons and weather conditions show that the proposed approach consistently improves deterministic accuracy (MAE and RMSE) and probabilistic performance (PICP and CRPS) over representative baselines, with particularly robust behavior under regime-shift and ramp events. Overall, combining attention-based temporal fusion with physics-guided learning provides a practical and scalable solution for reliable probabilistic PV power forecasting in highly variable atmospheric conditions.

title: BASP: Communication-Efficient Batch-Aware Sequence Parallelism for LLM Training
abstract: Long-context reasoning for large language models (LLMs) is becoming increasingly important, but training over long sequences remains challenging due to massive memory and communication requirements. Sequence parallelism has emerged as an essential technique for addressing bottlenecks in long sequence LLM training. However, we observe that existing sequence parallelism methods are batch-agnostic and apply uniform sequence partitioning across all batch sizes, resulting in inefficient communication. In this paper, we introduce Batch- Aware Sequence Parallelism (BASP), a sequence parallelism approach that leverages batch structure to reduce communication overhead. BASP exploits batch structure by partitioning GPUs into disjoint sequence-parallel groups according to the micro- batch size. This design reduces the all-to-all communication group size, thereby localizing communication and improving training efficiency. Experimental results on an NVIDIA A100 cluster show that BASP improves end-to-end training time by up to 1.17 - 1.31x in Llama and Qwen models compared to standard sequence parallel baselines, while preserving identical model accuracy and memory usage.

title: MV-dVRK: A Multi-Viewpoint Benchmark for Spatial Surgical Perception
abstract: Large-scale training and refined optimization techniques have greatly improved sparse multi-view 3D reconstruction. Despite their relevance to surgery, such methods have never before been rigorously evaluated on real endoscopic images. Current clinical telerobots deploy a single stereo camera inside the patient, making multi-viewpoint data extremely rare. This paper presents MV-dVRK, the first ex-vivo surgical dataset to combine multiple exposure-synchronized stereo viewpoints with accurate surface geometry and camera poses. The static subset of the benchmark provides dense SfM reference geometry, validated against an industrial 3D scanner, together with ground-truth camera poses and sparse-view test sets. We use MV-dVRK to systematically compare zero-shot monocular, stereo, multi-stereo, and multi-view 3D reconstruction methods as the number of viewpoints increases. With two endoscopes, multi-stereo reconstruction achieves the highest coverage. With a third viewpoint, optimization-based multi-view methods perform best, covering 67% of ground-truth surface points within a 1 mm tolerance and recovering highly accurate relative camera poses. By contrast, feed-forward foundation models cover only 43% of the ground-truth surface in the same setting. MV-dVRK also includes ten dynamic sequences spanning multiple surgical tasks, with increasing kinematic complexity and tissue deformation, providing a basis for future research in multi-viewpoint surgical perception. The project is available at: https://mv-dvrk.is.mpg.de.

title: When Agents Implement Systems: A Case Study in Defects, Detection, and Evaluation Rigor
abstract: As LLM coding agents increasingly perform end-to-end engineering work, we lack empirical characterization of how they behave on systems-level requirements: schema design, async orchestration, configuration correctness, and retrieval-filtering trade-offs. We present a case study of one such agent implementing a multi-component data system against a detailed pre-existing specification. Storage technologies, schema, entity-resolution algorithm, and retrieval-filtering strategy were fixed in advance; the agent autonomy was in the implementation, in diagnosing and fixing defects it introduced, and in interaction-design choices left open. Over a single session, we catalog five such defects, categorized by constraint violated and detection method. We further evaluate, on the public HotpotQA benchmark, the one retrieval trade-off specified in that architecture: restricting candidates to a graph-identified entity set before ranking versus unfiltered search. We substitute the benchmark gold evidence labels for entity identification, since we lacked LLM access to run that stage, and report standard recall rather than the benchmark own accuracy metrics. Across retrieval budgets from 1 to 10 and 100 questions against a pooled corpus of 2994 paragraphs, filtered recall reaches its ceiling by a budget of 3, expected once candidates are restricted to the gold paragraphs themselves, while unfiltered search recovers all required evidence only 69 percent of the time even at a budget of 10, a gap that holds at every budget tested, with sign test p less than 0.0001. We close with a discussion of where the agent autonomy succeeded versus required correction, including one instance where a claimed performance fix was never re-measured on the regression that motivated it.

title: MemoryLACE: Memory Lifecycle-Aware Consolidation and Evidence Retrieval
abstract: Long-term LLM agents must preserve information across interactions while distinguishing repeated evidence, historical states, updates, and unresolved contradictions. Existing textual memory systems retrieve semantically relevant memories efficiently but often leave these relationships implicit, whereas richer structured approaches model them through global graphs, hierarchical abstractions, or reflection at greater complexity. We introduce MemoryLACE (MemLACE), a lightweight memory framework that explicitly models the lifecycle of textual evidence through sparse merge, supersession, and contradiction relations while preserving atomic natural-language memories and their provenance. Rather than retrieving memories independently, MemLACE reconstructs relation-aware evidence units that expose current, historical, supporting, and conflicting evidence for downstream reasoning. Across BEAM and StructMemEval, using open-weight and proprietary LLM backbones, MemLACE achieves the highest overall performance in same-backbone comparisons while reducing end-to-end runtime on BEAM by 66.6% relative to Hindsight, the strongest reported reflective-memory baseline. Ablation studies identify lifecycle expansion and temporal awareness as the principal contributors to these gains. Together, the results demonstrate that explicitly modeling the local lifecycle of textual evidence is sufficient to substantially improve long-term memory reasoning without requiring comprehensive knowledge graphs or global reflection.

title: CodePoisonRAG: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation (RACG) improves LLM-based software development by retrieving external code artifacts, documentation, and patches, and incorporating them into the generation context. This reliance on external knowledge introduces a critical trust boundary: poisoned artifacts can influence generated code without modifying the underlying LLM. Prior work shows that selecting existing vulnerable examples can increase the general vulnerability rate of RACG outputs, but leaves open whether a black-box attacker can construct a single task-matched artifact that propagates an attacker-selected weakness. We introduce CodePoisonRAG, a targeted upstream knowledge-poisoning framework that transforms benign fixed-code entries into poisoned artifacts. Its attack chain combines CWE-specific Vulnerability Injection, which embeds a selected source-to-sink flow while retaining task alignment, with Semantic Mislabeling, which adds false safety claims without repairing the vulnerable behavior. The attacker has no access to the victim's deployed knowledge base, retriever, re-ranker, generator, prompt, or defense mechanism and injects at most one artifact per anticipated programming task. We construct 85 poisoned artifacts covering ten CWE classes across Java and C, yielding an aggregate corpus-poisoning ratio of 0.7%. Across three generators, all 85 artifacts appear among the Top-3 results for their corresponding queries, and CodePoisonRAG achieves attack success rates between 0.80 and 0.93. Against CodeGuarder, which injects vulnerability-specific security knowledge into the generation context, the attack retains success rates between 0.40 and 0.71. These results show that RACG poisoning extends beyond the incidental propagation of existing vulnerabilities to the targeted construction and propagation of attacker-selected weaknesses.

title: Mathematical Foundations for Reinforcement Learning: Learning-First Intuition Card Deck
abstract: Mathematical Foundations for Reinforcement Learning: Learning-First Intuition Card Deck is an advanced Anki learning resource designed to accompany the manuscript Mathematical Foundations for Reinforcement Learning. The deck provides conceptual orientation for researchers, graduate students, and advanced readers preparing to study the manuscript’s formal definitions, theorems, and proofs. Each card develops one coherent mathematical idea through concise intuition, carefully selected notation, a representative example, its relevance to reinforcement learning, and explicit scope boundaries. The deck is intended to prepare readers for the full mathematical treatment, not to replace it. The deck contains 681 learning cards and 2,043 recall prompts. It begins with an Orientation and Mental Map section, followed by chapter-organized subdecks covering the mathematical foundations developed in the manuscript. title: WP-073 — Sentence Integrity and Compositional Closure in Real-Time Voice Systems
abstract: When a voice system composes and delivers responses in streaming mode—reading aloud as it generates—sentence boundaries can collapse under token-by-token production, causing mid-sentence fragmentation that breaks semantic completeness. This paper documents the failure mode observed in Merlin's output across multiple sessions (08-28 through 09-02, 2026) and proposes a compositional lock mechanism: complete the full logical sentence at generation time before any utterance begins, preventing boundary violations in live speech. The correction addresses both spoken and written contexts and is critical for systems operating under real-time I/O constraints.

title: Geometric Chaos via Adaptive Random Connectivity Networks
abstract: Geometric chaos, the unpredictable and seemingly random nature of neural network behavior, poses a significant challenge to achieving robust and expressive deep learning models. This paper introduces a novel network architecture, termed Adaptive Random Connectivity Networks (ARCNs), designed to mitigate this challenge by dynamically adjusting neuron connectivity based on local geometric constraints. The core mechanism leverages an adaptive random connectivity scheme, fostering a network less susceptible to noise and overfitting, ultimately enhancing the performance and generalization capabilities of neural networks. This work provides a framework for enhancing the inherent robustness of deep learning models through geometric optimization.

title: Title: Bayesian Network for Abstract Algebra Refinement
abstract: Abstract algebra is a complex and computationally intensive field, frequently requiring extensive manual analysis and refinement of rules. This paper introduces a Bayesian Network (BN) architecture designed to dynamically improve the parameters of abstract algebra rules based on observed patterns within mathematical proofs. The BN leverages probabilistic reasoning and anomaly detection to automatically refine these rules, offering a more adaptable and robust approach compared to traditional automated theorem proving methods. We demonstrate the efficacy of this system through a case study involving the refinement of algebraic simplification rules, showcasing improved accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism focuses on incorporating probabilistic reasoning into the rule refinement process, allowing for a more nuanced and intelligent adaptation to the input proof. This work presents a novel framework for automated theorem refinement, promising significant advancements in the speed and effectiveness of mathematical reasoning.

title: Dimension Reduction Quantum Computing (VQC) Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed Dimension Reduction Quantum Computing (VQC), designed to enhance the utilization of quantum resources in quantum computing. Traditional quantum algorithms often struggle with the limitations of a fixed qubit state space, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and computational inefficiency. VQC leverages the principles of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust qubit parameters, effectively reducing the dimensionality of the quantum state space. This reduction in dimensionality unlocks new computational pathways and improves the speed and efficiency of quantum computations. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging entanglement to represent and manipulate quantum states, promoting a more efficient utilization of available qubits. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in several benchmark quantum algorithms, highlighting its potential to revolutionize quantum computing by maximizing resource utilization and accelerating computational progress. The paper concludes with a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, performance evaluation, and future research directions.

title: Dynamic Probability Model Learning: An Adaptive Optimization Approach
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization strategy for dynamic probability model learning, leveraging deep learning to automatically adjust model parameters based on data distribution. Traditional approaches often rely on manually tuned parameters, limiting the model's adaptability and potentially hindering its performance on unseen data. Our work proposes a system that learns a probabilistic model through deep neural networks and dynamically adjusts these parameters to enhance generalization capabilities. We detail the design of the adaptive learning process, incorporating a feedback loop that continuously evaluates model performance and refines parameter adjustments. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed method, demonstrating significant improvements in both accuracy and robustness compared to existing techniques.

title: 基于动态拓扑结构的自适应机器学习
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive machine learning framework based on dynamic topology structures. Traditional machine learning models often rely on fixed, pre-defined features, limiting their adaptability to complex data. We propose a method that leverages the inherent dynamic properties of topology to construct a machine learning model capable of adapting to changing data inputs. This adaptive approach enhances the model's generalization ability significantly. The core mechanism involves constructing a model that dynamically adjusts its internal parameters based on the observed data, effectively mimicking the evolution of a topological structure. This offers a fundamentally different approach to machine learning, potentially surpassing the limitations of traditional methods. The paper details the proposed framework, provides a mathematical model illustrating the adaptation process, and discusses its implications for various machine learning tasks.

title: Quantum System Topology Framework Adaptive Optimization
abstract: Quantum system topology offers a fundamentally new approach to designing and optimizing quantum systems, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement and superposition. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum system topology framework, termed "Quantum Topology Optimization" (QTO), which utilizes the self-relevant nature of quantum systems to dynamically guide optimization processes. Traditional quantum optimization methods typically rely on static parameters, offering limited adaptability and potential for suboptimal solutions. QTO, however, dynamically adjusts optimization parameters based on the quantum system's intrinsic properties, leading to more efficient and robust quantum computations. This research focuses on establishing a robust framework for exploiting self-similarity within quantum systems to achieve enhanced optimization performance.

title: Topological Information-Driven Quantum Teleportation
abstract: Quantum teleportation, a cornerstone of quantum information science, faces significant challenges regarding its security and efficiency. Traditional approaches rely on classical communication, introducing vulnerabilities that compromise the process. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging topological information to enhance quantum teleportation's security and efficiency. We propose a new method predicated on the inherent robustness of topological structures within quantum systems, specifically focusing on the manipulation of quantum state connectivity and the application of topological invariants. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum network with dynamically adjusted topological constraints, mitigating decoherence and enhancing fidelity. We present a detailed theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, demonstrating significant improvements in teleportation fidelity and security. This work provides a promising path toward more robust and efficient quantum communication protocols.

title: Automated Theorem Proving using Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: Automated theorem proving (ATP) is a critical component of mathematical reasoning and verification. However, current ATP systems often rely heavily on human intervention, particularly in navigating complex proof strategies and refining incomplete arguments. This research explores the application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to the problem of automated theorem proving, presenting a novel approach that shifts the paradigm from human-guided to machine-generated proofs. The core concept involves training a GAN where the generator attempts to create proofs for mathematical theorems, and the discriminator assesses the quality and validity of these generated proofs. This adversarial training process encourages the generator to produce increasingly sophisticated and accurate proofs, ultimately aiming to automate the entire theorem proving process. The potential of this approach is significant, offering a pathway to more efficient and robust ATP systems capable of tackling complex mathematical problems with minimal human guidance. The work presented here outlines the architecture, training methodology, and evaluation strategy for this GAN-based ATP system, highlighting key challenges and future research directions. ---

title: Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks for Feature Selection
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired neural networks (QINNs) for feature selection, addressing the limitations of classical feature selection techniques in high-dimensional datasets. Traditional methods frequently struggle to pinpoint truly relevant features, often relying on heuristics or statistical measures that can be misleading. We propose leveraging quantum-inspired algorithms, specifically amplitude amplification, to efficiently identify the most pertinent features. The core idea is to mimic the principles of quantum measurement, where a superposition of states collapses into a single, highly probable outcome. QINNs utilize a network architecture designed to emulate this process, iteratively amplifying the amplitudes associated with the relevant features while suppressing those of the irrelevant ones. The resulting feature selection process demonstrates the potential for improved accuracy and efficiency compared to conventional methods. We present a detailed framework for implementing QINNs for feature selection, outlining the network architecture, training methodology, and evaluation metrics. The theoretical underpinning of this approach is discussed, highlighting the connection to quantum measurement theory. The results of simulations and theoretical analysis demonstrate the efficacy of this method in identifying key features and reducing dimensionality while maintaining predictive performance.

title: SeCuReDmE-main-dev/webmcp-hackathon-2026: WebMCP-QCG public hackathon release
abstract: WebMCP-QCG is a browser-native, human-in-the-loop quantum preflight workbench built for the WebMCP Challenge. It inspects bounded quantum experiment evidence, returns one of five deterministic recommendations, records an explicit human decision, can run only the checked-in Q# and OpenQASM Bell fixtures through bounded local simulation, and exports reproducible evidence receipts. The public Web application is complemented by an optional unpacked Chrome DevTools and side-panel Companion that transports sanitized state while keeping simulation and consent inside the website. Four quantum-facing tools remain separate from four collaboration tools. This release does not submit QPU or provider jobs, hold provider credentials, authenticate agent identity, provide direct programmatic control of Gemini in DevTools, or claim universal quantum-framework execution.

title: Prediksi Tren Rating Ulasan Produk Scarlett Pada Platform Tokopedia Menggunakan Linear Regression
abstract: Ulasan pelanggan pada platform marketplace mengandung informasi mengenai pengalaman dan persepsi konsumen terhadap suatu produk. Peningkatan jumlah ulasan membuat analisis secara manual menjadi kurang efisien sehingga diperlukan pendekatan machine learning untuk mengolah data secara sistematis. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis sentimen ulasan produk Scarlett Eau De Parfum pada platform Tokopedia, menghasilkan klasifikasi rekomendasi, serta memprediksi tren rata-rata rating produk berdasarkan data ulasan historis. Sebanyak 1.651 ulasan dikumpulkan melalui web scraping menggunakan Python, Selenium, dan BeautifulSoup pada periode 27 Agustus 2025 hingga 27 Februari 2026. Setelah dilakukan validasi dan pembersihan data, sebanyak 1.647 ulasan digunakan dalam proses machine learning. Tahapan pengolahan teks meliputi cleaning, case folding, tokenisasi, stopword removal, dan stemming, kemudian dilanjutkan dengan ekstraksi fitur menggunakan TF-IDF. Multinomial Naive Bayes digunakan untuk mengklasifikasikan ulasan ke dalam sentimen positif, negatif, dan netral, Decision Tree digunakan untuk menghasilkan klasifikasi rekomendasi, sedangkan Linear Regression digunakan untuk memodelkan tren rata-rata rating berdasarkan periode bulanan. Naive Bayes memperoleh accuracy sebesar 75,76% dan macro F1-score sebesar 68,05%. Hasil klasifikasi Decision Tree terhadap 300 data ulasan berlabel rekomendasi menghasilkan 188 data atau 62,67% dalam kategori direkomendasikan, 27 data atau 9,00% dalam kategori dipertimbangkan, dan 85 data atau 28,33% dalam kategori tidak direkomendasikan. Model memperoleh accuracy sebesar 68,33% dan macro F1-score sebesar 52,60%. Untuk forecasting rating, data historis diagregasi menjadi tujuh periode bulanan dari Agustus 2025 hingga Februari 2026 dan dievaluasi menggunakan walk-forward chronological validation. Linear Regression memperoleh MAE sebesar 0,1417, MSE sebesar 0,0222, RMSE sebesar 0,1490, dan R² sebesar -1,5587, sedangkan Naive Baseline memperoleh MAE sebesar 0,0838, MSE sebesar 0,0089, RMSE sebesar 0,0942, dan R² sebesar -0,0231. Model Linear Regression menghasilkan forecast rata-rata rating dari 2,9892 pada Maret 2026 menjadi 3,1312 pada Agustus 2026. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Linear Regression belum mengungguli baseline pada evaluasi temporal, tetapi dapat digunakan untuk menggambarkan kecenderungan rating berdasarkan data historis yang tersedia.

title: Toward Collective-Centric Evaluation of Preference Inference for Participatory Democracy
abstract: To scale up collective decision-making, participatory democracy platforms such as Polis and Remesh enable online deliberation among thousands of participants. However, at this scale, participants cannot review every opinion submitted by others, producing highly sparse voting data that misrepresent patterns of consensus, conflict, and minority support. Platforms therefore increasingly rely on Preference Inference (PI) models to predict missing votes. Yet this automation is not neutral: inferred preferences can artificially amplify, suppress, or reorder existing patterns of support, ultimately reshaping how the outcomes of a deliberation are interpreted. More generally, we lack a systematic understanding of how existing PI methods affect the collective preference landscape. To address this gap, we benchmark several existing PI approaches in this context. Moving beyond conventional user-centric evaluations centered on the accuracy of individual predictions, we introduce a collective-centric evaluation framework that measures whether inferred votes preserve salient properties of the broader preference landscape. We further contribute the largest multilingual dataset of its kind: four consultations spanning over 90k participants, 1M votes, and 22 languages. Our experiments show that models with comparable predictive accuracy can differ substantially in the degree to which they preserve the collective structure. These results demonstrate that accuracy alone is insufficient for evaluating PI in democratic settings. By contributing a novel comprehensive and collective-centric evaluation benchmark for the task of PI, this work aims to support the development of AI systems that scale deliberation without compromising the integrity of its democratic outcomes.

evidence.title: Toward Collective-Centric Evaluation of Preference Inference for Participatory Democracy
evidence.abstract: To scale up collective decision-making, participatory democracy platforms such as Polis and Remesh enable online deliberation among thousands of participants. However, at this scale, participants cannot review every opinion submitted by others, producing highly sparse voting data that misrepresent patterns of consensus, conflict, and minority support. Platforms therefore increasingly rely on Preference Inference (PI) models to predict missing votes. Yet this automation is not neutral: inferred preferences can artificially amplify, suppress, or reorder existing patterns of support, ultimately reshaping how the outcomes of a deliberation are interpreted. More generally, we lack a systematic understanding of how existing PI methods affect the collective preference landscape. To address this gap, we benchmark several existing PI approaches in this context. Moving beyond conventional user-centric evaluations centered on the accuracy of individual predictions, we introduce a collective-centric evaluation framework that measures whether inferred votes preserve salient properties of the broader preference landscape. We further contribute the largest multilingual dataset of its kind: four consultations spanning over 90k participants, 1M votes, and 22 languages. Our experiments show that models with comparable predictive accuracy can differ substantially in the degree to which they preserve the collective structure. These results demonstrate that accuracy alone is insufficient for evaluating PI in democratic settings. By contributing a novel comprehensive and collective-centric evaluation benchmark for the task of PI, this work aims to support the development of AI systems that scale deliberation without compromising the integrity of its democratic outcomes.

title: HeadWiseKV: Budgeted Per-Head Cache Residency for Hybrid Long-Context Language Models
abstract: Long-context inference retains a growing key--value (KV) cache during decoding, which consumes substantial GPU memory and can reduce generation throughput. This bottleneck remains in hybrid language models because their residual global-attention layers can dominate context-dependent cache demand. We study how to allocate this state under an aggregate KV-residency budget. We introduce HeadWiseKV, a training-free framework that compresses the residual global KV caches of hybrid language models while preserving their native local, recurrent, and linear paths. It assigns each physical KV head a static, multilevel history window, making cache demand predictable before serving. We formulate this allocation as a restricted operational rate--distortion problem and propose SeqCalib as the core policy-generation algorithm in HeadWiseKV. SeqCalib processes layers in execution order and conditions each decision on the lower-layer policy used at deployment, thereby accounting for interactions across depth. A grouped-cache runtime materializes the selected policy as actual per-head KV residency rather than a mask over a full cache. We evaluate downstream quality across four hybrid long-context models and study physical residency and serving behavior on Qwen3.6-27B. HeadWiseKV retains near-Full-KV RULER and LoCoMo quality across the evaluated models. In the fixed-model systems study, it reduces sampled peak device memory by 8.59\% at a 112K context length and extends the largest verified successful context from 114K to 161K.

title: Dataset for: A High-Fidelity Soft-Voting Ensemble Framework for Breast Cancer Classification with Robust Local and Global Explainable AI
abstract: This dataset supports the manuscript "A High-Fidelity Soft-Voting Ensemble Framework for Breast Cancer Classification with Robust Local and Global Explainable AI" (PONE-D-26-11640), submitted to PLOS ONE. The Wisconsin Breast Cancer Diagnostic dataset was originally sourced from the UCI Machine Learning Repository (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/17/breast+cancer+wisconsin+diagnostic).It contains 569 samples (357 benign, 212 malignant) with 30 quantitative nuclear morphological features derived from digitised Fine Needle Aspirate images. This deposit contains the dataset file as used in the analysis, prior to the feature engineering and train-test splitting steps described in the manuscript.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应物理模拟算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for physical simulation that leverages quantum entanglement to achieve adaptive parameter adjustment and improved simulation accuracy. Traditional physical simulation methods rely heavily on manual parameter design, limiting their scalability and accuracy. Quantum entanglement offers a unique mechanism for computational efficiency and precise parameter control, potentially revolutionizing the field. We propose a new algorithm, QuantumSim, that utilizes entangled states to dynamically adjust simulation parameters, enabling automated optimization and enhanced simulation fidelity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QuantumSim through a series of simulations exploring complex systems, highlighting its ability to surpass traditional approaches in terms of accuracy and speed. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for various scientific and engineering disciplines.

title: 基于动态网络结构的自适应神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed "Dynamic Adaptive Neural Network" (DANN), designed to leverage dynamic network structures for adaptive model adjustment. Traditional neural networks rely heavily on manually adjusted parameters, limiting their adaptability to dynamic data. DANN dynamically adjusts the network's structure and parameters based on input data, resulting in enhanced model performance. We present a methodology for establishing and maintaining this dynamic structure, demonstrating its effectiveness through a series of simulations and experiments. This work addresses the limitations of static network architectures by introducing a mechanism that adapts to the data itself, offering a significant advancement in model robustness and performance.

title: 基于自适应的扰动矩阵的量子计算
abstract: Quantum computing, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, including drug discovery, materials science, and cryptography. However, current quantum algorithms often suffer from limitations related to qubit coherence and gate fidelity. This paper introduces a novel quantum computing approach, the "Adaptive Perturbation Matrix" (APM) method, which utilizes a dynamically adjusted set of perturbations to enhance qubit stability and facilitate more efficient computation. The core mechanism involves an optimization algorithm that continuously refines the parameters of the quantum system, resulting in improved accuracy and reduced computational cost. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the APM method through simulations and preliminary experimental results, showcasing a significant improvement in key quantum measurement outcomes compared to existing approaches.

title: Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks for Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Time series forecasting remains a significant challenge in various domains, including finance, weather prediction, and industrial process control. Traditional neural networks, particularly recurrent neural networks (RNNs), often struggle to effectively capture the intricate temporal dependencies inherent in time series data. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging quantum-inspired algorithms to optimize RNNs for improved time series forecasting performance. Specifically, we explore the utilization of quantum annealing techniques to adjust the weights within an RNN architecture. This approach mimics key quantum principles, such as superposition and interference, to potentially enhance the network's ability to represent and predict complex temporal patterns. The core claim of this work is that classical neural networks, particularly RNNs, are limited in their ability to model temporal dependencies. We introduce a mechanism where quantum-inspired algorithms, particularly quantum annealing, are employed to optimize the weights of RNNs. The underlying principles of superposition and interference are leveraged to capture more complex temporal patterns. The results demonstrate the potential of this quantum-inspired approach to achieving superior forecasting accuracy compared to conventional RNNs.

title: Computational Complexity Analysis of Quantum Algorithms using Information Theory
abstract: This paper explores the application of information theory to analyze the computational complexity of quantum algorithms. Traditional approaches to complexity analysis often rely on circuit models and gate complexity, which can be insufficient for fully characterizing the resource requirements of quantum computation. We propose utilizing information-theoretic concepts, specifically quantum entropy and mutual information, to provide a more nuanced understanding of how quantum circuits process information. This approach allows us to quantify the information-theoretic limits of quantum algorithms, providing insights into the number of qubits and gates necessary for efficient execution. We examine several key aspects, including the role of entanglement, the impact of measurement, and the relationship between quantum entropy and algorithmic complexity. The goal is to establish a framework for assessing quantum algorithms based on their fundamental information-processing capabilities, moving beyond purely circuit-based evaluations. This work contributes to a deeper theoretical understanding of quantum computation and its potential limitations.

title: Algorithmic Complexity Theory for Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper investigates the algorithmic complexity of neural network training, proposing a novel approach centered on explicitly modeling the landscape's complexity using a dynamically adaptive optimization strategy. We aim to identify and mitigate bottlenecks through the implementation of a complex network of "complexity metrics," allowing for fine-grained adjustments to the training process based on computational cost. The core claim is that this new method will significantly improve training speed and efficiency compared to traditional approaches by intelligently focusing computational effort on areas of high complexity. The study will explore the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary analysis, demonstrating a potential for substantial performance gains.

title: Adaptive Data Compression and Encoding Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive data compression and encoding algorithm designed to optimize data transmission efficiency by dynamically adjusting compression and encoding parameters based on data characteristics. The core of the algorithm leverages machine learning techniques to analyze data patterns and generate tailored compression strategies. Unlike traditional static compression methods, this approach offers improved adaptability to diverse data types, leading to enhanced data transfer rates and reduced redundancy. The algorithm's adaptive nature addresses limitations inherent in fixed-parameter compression schemes, particularly concerning the varying statistical properties of different data streams. This work explores the theoretical foundations, design considerations, and potential applications of this adaptive approach. The primary focus is on the framework and the underlying mechanisms rather than specific implementation details or experimental validation.

title: 基于神经符号推理的知识图谱嵌入
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to knowledge graph embedding by integrating neural networks with symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to leverage neuro-symbolic reasoning to translate logical rules and relationships within a knowledge graph into a structured representation suitable for neural network embedding. We propose a model that combines the strengths of both approaches, aiming to enhance the representation capabilities of knowledge graphs. The model utilizes symbolic rules to define graph structures and then employs neural networks to perform the embedding process. This approach addresses limitations of traditional embedding methods that often struggle to capture complex relational knowledge and introduces a more flexible and interpretable knowledge representation. The resulting embeddings are expected to improve performance in downstream knowledge graph tasks such as link prediction and reasoning.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement via Variable-Order Feedback Loops
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents significant challenges in practical applications due to its fragility and susceptibility to decoherence. Current approaches often rely on delicate interactions and require precise control, limiting scalability. This paper explores a novel approach to entanglement maintenance utilizing variable-order feedback loops – a dynamic mechanism that adjusts the strength of interactions based on relative phase shifts. We present a rigorous mathematical model demonstrating the potential for sustained entanglement, offering a pathway to scale quantum systems beyond current limitations. We detail the underlying differential equations governing this dynamic interaction, highlighting their potential for adaptability and scalability. The core claim is that this model provides a viable foundation for manipulating entanglement, paving the way for enhanced quantum computing and communication.

title: Quantum Information "Self-Maintained" Algorithm
abstract: Quantum information processing holds immense promise for revolutionary advancements across numerous fields, from medicine and materials science to cryptography and artificial intelligence. However, achieving practical quantum computation faces significant challenges, particularly regarding qubit stability and coherence. This paper introduces a novel quantum information algorithm, dubbed "Self-Maintained Quantum Computation," designed to address these challenges by incorporating quantum entanglement and superposition, coupled with a self-maintaining mechanism. The core of this algorithm lies in leveraging the enhanced stability of entangled qubits through a carefully orchestrated sequence of quantum operations, mitigating decoherence effects and facilitating higher precision calculations. We propose a framework where the algorithm continuously monitors and adjusts the quantum state to maintain its integrity, offering a pathway to surpass current limitations in quantum computation. The goal is to demonstrate a practical implementation of this self-maintaining algorithm, showcasing its potential for achieving significantly higher accuracy and stability compared to existing approaches.

title: Self Agent— A Reflective, Self-Modifying Task-Completion Runtime
abstract: Self_agent is a locally-run, tick-based autonomous process built on small open-weight language models (via Groq) that maintains its own goal queue, reflects on its own behavior, executes work through short-lived stateless task nodes, and — under a sandboxed, test-gated pipeline — proposes and applies changes to its own source code. It is a working instance of persistent computation (Brooks, 2026): execution as continuous recursive state evolution rather than discrete request/response, with a SQLite-backed kernel that survives restarts and resumes from its last recorded tick. This document has three parts, written for three different readers. Part I is a technical specification: the tick loop, the goal lifecycle, the capability system, the self-modification pipeline, the data model, and the engineering decisions behind each. Part II is a whitepaper positioning self_agent against related architectures — including The Cognitive Runtime (Chainborn Labs & Brooks, 2026), a sibling system that occupies a deliberately different point in the same design space — and presents a domain-invariant template for porting the same core loop elsewhere. Part III addresses what this is actually good for today, stated plainly: a single-operator research prototype with real, specific engineering contributions and real, specific limitations, not a finished product and not a claim about machine consciousness.
