title: Distributed Neuron Networks: A Dynamical Systems Perspective
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of information flow within distributed neuron networks, proposing a novel approach to designing more efficient neural architectures. We utilize non-equilibrium dynamical systems theory to model the evolution of information propagation in neural networks, exploring strategies for controlling this flow. The core claim is that understanding the dynamical behavior of information flow is crucial for optimizing distributed neural networks. We move beyond the traditional view of neurons as isolated computational units and treat the network as a dynamic system governed by non-equilibrium principles. The key mechanisms involve analyzing the system's response to perturbations and identifying control parameters that can steer information towards desired states. This research provides a theoretical framework for understanding and manipulating information flow in complex neural systems, with potential implications for a wide range of applications, including artificial intelligence, neuroscience, and distributed computing. The analysis focuses on the evolution of the network's state, represented mathematically through appropriate differential equations. This work establishes a foundation for future research into adaptive and robust neural networks.

title: Adaptive Symbolic Evolution System (ASES)
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Symbolic Evolution System (ASES), a novel approach to software optimization that leverages evolutionary computation to automatically discover and refine symbolic representations of software code. The core premise is that by mimicking the process of biological evolution, ASES can effectively optimize code for improved readability, maintainability, and performance. The system operates by treating software code as a "population" of individual implementations. Utilizing a genetic algorithm with operations such as crossover and mutation, ASES generates new code implementations, which are then evaluated based on performance metrics. The most promising implementations are selected for reproduction, while less effective ones are eliminated, leading to the eventual emergence of optimized code. This automated, adaptive approach contrasts sharply with traditional software optimization techniques, offering the potential for discovering optimal code representations without manual intervention and adapting to evolving requirements. The system's key innovation lies in its ability to continuously refine the symbolic representation of the code, leading to potentially significant improvements in various software aspects.

The system's key innovation lies in its ability to continuously refine the symbolic representation of the code, leading to potentially significant improvements in various software aspects.

title: Based on Genetic Algorithm for Compiler Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of genetic algorithms (GAs) to optimize compilers. Traditional compiler optimization relies heavily on hand-crafted heuristics and algorithms, often requiring significant expert knowledge and extensive manual tuning. This approach can be time-consuming and may not always yield the most effective optimization strategies. This research proposes a novel framework where compiler optimization problems are modeled as optimization problems solvable by GAs. The core of the approach involves encoding different optimization strategies as chromosomes within a GA population. Through iterative selection, crossover, and mutation, the GA explores the solution space, ultimately converging on optimization strategies that can demonstrably improve compilation efficiency and code quality. We present a detailed methodology, including chromosome representation, fitness function design, and GA parameter tuning, focusing on the potential of GAs to automate and enhance the compiler optimization process. The results presented demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach, suggesting a promising avenue for future compiler development.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Fractal Simulation (QESF)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Fractal Simulation (QESF) is a novel computational technique designed to accelerate and improve the simulation of fractal structures by integrating quantum computation. This research investigates the potential of leveraging quantum algorithms to represent and manipulate fractal patterns, aiming to surpass the limitations of traditional classical methods in terms of fidelity and computational speed. The core mechanism centers on utilizing quantum entanglement to enhance the representation and traversal of fractal geometries, ultimately achieving a higher degree of accuracy and efficiency in the simulation process. This paper explores the theoretical underpinnings of QESF, outlines the key algorithmic components, and presents preliminary results demonstrating the potential for substantial speedups compared to classical methods. The study focuses primarily on the representation of fractal patterns using quantum states and explores the application of quantum entanglement to enhance the simulation of complex fractal geometries. The ultimate goal is to establish QESF as a viable and powerful tool for modeling and simulating fractal structures across various scientific and engineering disciplines.

title: Conclusions
abstract: The analyses presented throughout this book demonstrate that artificial intelligence is no longer limited to the role of a technological support mechanism operating at the margins of organisational activity. Instead, AI increasingly functions as an integrated element of enterprise structures, influencing how organisations process information, coordinate activities, formulate strategies, manage operations, and distribute decision-making authority. The transition from AI-support enterprises towards AI-first enterprises reflects a broader transformation in organisational logic, where algorithmic systems become embedded within the core mechanisms of governance and management. As noted by Dignum (2019) , the growing organisational role of AI requires enterprises to rethink not only technological infrastructures but also institutional responsibility, ethical governance, and managerial control.

title: Figure 4 from Counterfactual Diffusion Models Provide Interpretable Explanations of Artificial Intelligence Models in Pathology
abstract: Independent classifier validation and representative bidirectional counterfactual transformations in a multiclass setting. A, External classifier responses to counterfactual morphing. Counterfactual images were generated at increasing morphing amplitudes (α) with MoPaDi and then encoded with three foundation models (UNI2, CONCH, and Virchow2). Independent classifiers were trained on the corresponding encoders’ features extracted from all TCGA-CRC tiles and then used to predict the target probability P(target) on both the original and counterfactual tiles. The resulting change ΔP(target) reflects how strongly the morphing affected class evidence. Bars show the median ΔP(target) with percentile-based variability across tiles. B, Representative examples of bidirectional counterfactual explanations for MSIL patients. We defined MSIL by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture model to the log-transformed distribution of total MSI events and using the intersection of the two components as the cutoff separating MSIL from MSIH samples.
